# zen

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/README.md

# zen

**Zen** is a props-driven React component library built for speed. Build polished interfaces without writing HTML, CSS, or thinking about Tailwind classes.

- **Props over classes** - Style through component props, not utility classes
- **Design included** - Complete design system out of the box with dark mode
- **Accessible** - Built on [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/) primitives
- **Powered by Tailwind** - Uses [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) under the hood, but you never touch it

[Documentation](https://zen.umami.is/)

## Installation

```shell
npm install @umami/react-zen
```

## Usage

### Import styles

```javascript
import '@umami/react-zen/styles.css';
```

### Build with components

```jsx
import { Box, Column, Heading, Text, Button } from '@umami/react-zen';

export default function Welcome() {
  return (
    <Box padding="6" border borderRadius="lg" shadow="lg">
      <Column alignItems="center" gap="6">
        <Heading size="3xl">Welcome</Heading>
        <Text color="muted">This is the zen way.</Text>
        <Button variant="primary">Enter</Button>
      </Column>
    </Box>
  );
}
```

No `className`. No CSS files. Just components and props.

## Why Zen?

Building UI is slow. You have to think about markup, CSS organization, responsive breakpoints, accessibility, and design consistency.

Zen eliminates that friction:

| Traditional approach | zen approach |
|---------------------|--------------|
| Write HTML structure | Compose components |
| Add Tailwind classes | Pass props |
| Handle responsive manually | Use responsive objects |
| Configure accessibility | Already done |

## Development

This is a Turborepo monorepo with:
- `packages/react-zen` - Component library
- `apps/docs` - Documentation site

### Build the component library

```bash
pnpm --filter @umami/react-zen build
```

### Run the docs site

```bash
pnpm --filter react-zen-docs dev
```

Runs on http://localhost:9001

### Build everything

```bash
pnpm build
```

### Lint

```bash
pnpm lint
```

# Breadcrumbs

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/breadcrumbs.mdx

title: Breadcrumbs

# Breadcrumbs

Breadcrumbs display a hierarchy of links to the current page or resource in an application.

  <Breadcrumbs>
    <Breadcrumb>
      <a href="#">Home</a>
    </Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb>
      <a href="#">One</a>
    </Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb>
      <a href="#">Two</a>
    </Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb>Three</Breadcrumb>
  </Breadcrumbs>

  ```jsx
  <Breadcrumbs>
    <Breadcrumb><a href="#">Home</a></Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb><a href="#">One</a></Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb><a href="#">Two</a></Breadcrumb>
    <Breadcrumb>Three</Breadcrumb>
  </Breadcrumbs>
  ```

## Component props

### Breadcrumbs

      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables all breadcrumbs' },
      { name: 'onAction', value: '(key: string) => void', description: 'Called when a breadcrumb is clicked' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Breadcrumb

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Unique breadcrumb identifier' },
      { name: 'href', value: 'string', description: 'Link URL' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the breadcrumb' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Button

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/button.mdx

title: Button

# Button

A button allows a user to perform an action, with mouse, touch, and keyboard interactions.

  <Button variant="primary">Button</Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button variant="primary">Button</Button>
  ```

## Variants

<Example direction="row">
  <Button variant="primary">Primary</Button>
  <Button>Default</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Outline</Button>
  <Button variant="quiet">Quiet</Button>
  <Button variant="danger">Danger</Button>
  <Button variant="zero">Zero</Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button variant="primary">Primary</Button>
  <Button>Default</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Outline</Button>
  <Button variant="quiet">Quiet</Button>
  <Button variant="danger">Danger</Button>
  <Button variant="zero">Zero</Button>
  ```

## Sizes

<Example direction="row">
  <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
  <Button size="md">Medium</Button>
  <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
  <Button size="xl">X-Large</Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
  <Button size="md">Medium</Button>
  <Button size="lg">Large</Button>
  <Button size="xl">X-Large</Button>
  ```

## Disabled

<Example direction="row">
  <Button isDisabled variant="primary">Primary</Button>
  <Button isDisabled>Default</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="outline">Outline</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="quiet">Quiet</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="danger">Danger</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="zero">Zero</Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button isDisabled variant="primary">Primary</Button>
  <Button isDisabled>Default</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="outline">Outline</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="quiet">Quiet</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="danger">Danger</Button>
  <Button isDisabled variant="zero">Zero</Button>
  ```

## Icon

<Example direction="row">
  <Button variant="primary">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button>
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="quiet">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="danger">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="zero">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button variant="primary">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button>
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="outline">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="quiet">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="danger">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  <Button variant="zero">
    <Icon size="sm">
      <Lucide.File />
    </Icon>
  </Button>
  ```

## Render as link

  <Button render={<a href="#" />}>
    Button as a link
  </Button>

  ```jsx
  <Button render={<a href="#" />}>
    Button as a link
  </Button>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'variant', value: 'ButtonVariant', description: '"default" | "primary" | "outline" | "quiet" | "danger" | "zero"' },
      { name: 'size', value: 'ButtonSize', description: '"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" (default: "md")' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the button' },
      { name: 'render', value: 'RenderProp', description: 'Render prop for polymorphism (e.g., render as link)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Hover Trigger

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/hover-trigger.mdx

title: Hover Trigger

# Hover Trigger

Displays a popover element when a user hovers over a trigger element.

<Example direction="row">
  <HoverTrigger>
    <Button variant="primary">Hover Me</Button>
    <Dialog>
      <Column gap="3">
        <Switch defaultSelected>Wi-Fi</Switch>
        <Switch defaultSelected>Bluetooth</Switch>
        <Switch>Mute</Switch>
      </Column>
    </Dialog>
  </HoverTrigger>

  ```jsx
  <HoverTrigger>
    <Button variant="primary">Hover Me</Button>
    <Dialog>
      <Column gap="3">
        <Switch defaultSelected>Wi-Fi</Switch>
        <Switch defaultSelected>Bluetooth</Switch>
        <Switch>Mute</Switch>
      </Column>
    </Dialog>
  </HoverTrigger>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'isOpen', value: 'boolean', description: 'Controlled open state' },
      { name: 'closeDelay', value: 'number', description: 'Delay before closing in ms (default: 500)' },
      { name: 'onHoverStart', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when hover starts' },
      { name: 'onHoverEnd', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when hover ends' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Loading Button

A button that indicates an action is still pending.

  <LoadingButton isLoading />

  ```jsx
  <LoadingButton isLoading />
  ```

## With text

  <LoadingButton isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>

  ```jsx
  <LoadingButton isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  ```

## Variants

  <LoadingButton variant="primary" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="outline" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="quiet" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="danger" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>

  ```jsx
  <LoadingButton variant="primary" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="outline" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="quiet" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="danger" isLoading>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  ```

## Disabled

  <LoadingButton variant="primary" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="outline" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="quiet" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="danger" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>

  ```jsx
  <LoadingButton variant="primary" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="outline" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="quiet" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  <LoadingButton variant="danger" isLoading isDisabled>Loading...</LoadingButton>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'isLoading', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows loading indicator' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'ButtonVariant', description: '"default" | "primary" | "outline" | "quiet" | "danger"' },
      { name: 'size', value: 'ButtonSize', description: '"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the button' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Menu

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/menu.mdx

title: Menu

# Menu

A menu displays a list of actions or options that a user can choose.

  <Menu>
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Four</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Five</MenuItem>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Separators

  <Menu>
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuSeparator />
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Four</MenuItem>
    <MenuSeparator />
    <MenuItem>Five</MenuItem>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuSeparator />
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Sections

  <Menu>
    <MenuSection title="Introduction">
      <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    </MenuSection>
    <MenuSection title="Summary">
      <MenuItem>Four</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Five</MenuItem>
    </MenuSection>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu>
    <MenuSection title="Introduction">
      <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
      <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    </MenuSection>
    <MenuSection title="Summary">
      <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    </MenuSection>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Single select

  <Menu selectionMode="single">
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Four</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Five</MenuItem>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu selectionMode="single">
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Multiple select

  <Menu selectionMode="multiple">
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Four</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Five</MenuItem>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu selectionMode="multiple">
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem>Three</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Preselected

  <Menu selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['three', 'five']}>
    <MenuItem id="one">One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="two">Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="three">Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="four">Four</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="five">Five</MenuItem>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['three', 'five']}>
    <MenuItem id="one">One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="two">Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="three">Three</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Submenu

  <Menu>
    <MenuItem id="one">One</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="two">Two</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="three">Three</MenuItem>
    <MenuItem id="four">Four</MenuItem>
    <SubMenuTrigger>
      <MenuItem id="five" showSubMenuIcon>Five</MenuItem>
      <Popover>
        <Menu>
          <MenuItem id="six">Six</MenuItem>
          <MenuItem id="seven">Seven</MenuItem>
          <MenuItem id="eight">Eight</MenuItem>
        </Menu>
      </Popover>
    </SubMenuTrigger>
  </Menu>

  ```jsx
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem>One</MenuItem>
    <SubMenuTrigger>
      <MenuItem showSubMenuIcon>More</MenuItem>
      <Popover>
        <Menu>
          <MenuItem>Sub item 1</MenuItem>
          <MenuItem>Sub item 2</MenuItem>
        </Menu>
      </Popover>
    </SubMenuTrigger>
  </Menu>
  ```

## Component props

### Menu

      { name: 'selectionMode', value: 'SelectionMode', description: '"none" | "single" | "multiple"' },
      { name: 'selectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Controlled selected keys' },
      { name: 'defaultSelectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Default selected keys' },
      { name: 'onSelectionChange', value: '(keys: Selection) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### MenuItem

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Unique item identifier' },
      { name: 'icon', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Icon displayed before label' },
      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Item label text' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the item' },
      { name: 'showChecked', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows check mark when selected (default: true)' },
      { name: 'showSubMenuIcon', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows submenu arrow icon' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Navbar

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/navbar.mdx

title: Navbar

# Navbar

A horizontal navigation bar for website headers. Supports dropdown menus, links, and nested navigation items with hover and focus interactions for accessible site navigation.

  <Navbar>
    <NavbarItem label="Product">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>Features</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Pricing</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem label="Resources">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>Documentation</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>API Reference</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Support</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem label="Company">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>About</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Blog</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Careers</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem>
      <a href="https://github.com/umami-software/umami">GitHub</a>
    </NavbarItem>

  </Navbar>

  ```jsx
  <Navbar>
    <NavbarItem label="Product">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>Features</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Pricing</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem label="Resources">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>Documentation</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>API Reference</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Support</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem label="Company">
      <Menu>
        <MenuItem>About</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Blog</MenuItem>
        <MenuItem>Careers</MenuItem>
      </Menu>
    </NavbarItem>
    <NavbarItem>
      <a href="https://github.com/umami-software/umami">GitHub</a>
    </NavbarItem>
  </Navbar>
  ```

## Component props

### Navbar

      { name: 'showArrow', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows dropdown arrow on items (default: true)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### NavbarItem

      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Item label (enables hover dropdown)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Palette Switcher

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/palette-switcher.mdx

title: Palette Switcher

# Palette Switcher

A segmented control that allows users to choose between different color palettes (neutral, slate, gray, zinc, stone).

  <PaletteSwitcher />

  ```jsx
  <PaletteSwitcher />
  ```

## Features

- Shows all five palette options at once
- Highlights the currently selected palette
- Persists the palette preference to `localStorage` under `zen.palette`
- Changes apply instantly via CSS custom properties

## Available palettes

      { name: 'neutral', description: 'Pure gray with no color tint (default)' },
      { name: 'slate', description: 'Cool blue-gray tones' },
      { name: 'gray', description: 'Slight blue tint' },
      { name: 'zinc', description: 'Subtle blue undertones' },
      { name: 'stone', description: 'Warm tan/brown tones' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Palette" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

## Programmatic usage

Use the `useTheme` hook to control the palette programmatically.

```jsx
import { useTheme } from '@umami/react-zen';

function MyComponent() {
  const { palette, setPalette } = useTheme();

  return (
    <Button onPress={() => setPalette('slate')}>
      Current palette: {palette}
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## With ZenProvider

Set the default palette for your application.

```jsx
import { ZenProvider } from '@umami/react-zen';

function App() {
  return (
    <ZenProvider palette="slate">
      <YourApp />
    </ZenProvider>
  );
}
```

## Component props

      { name: 'className', value: 'string', description: 'Additional CSS classes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

---

# Tabs

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/tabs.mdx

title: Tabs

# Tabs

Tabs organize content into multiple sections and allow users to navigate between them.

  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three">Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>

  ```jsx
  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three">Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>
  ```

## Disabled

  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three" isDisabled>Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>

  ```jsx
  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three" isDisabled>Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>
  ```

## With links

  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one" href="#one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two" href="#two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three" href="#three">Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>

  ```jsx
  <Tabs>
    <TabList>
      <Tab id="one" href="#one">One</Tab>
      <Tab id="two" href="#two">Two</Tab>
      <Tab id="three" href="#three">Three</Tab>
    </TabList>
    <TabPanel id="one">Content for tab one.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="two">Content for tab two.</TabPanel>
    <TabPanel id="three">Content for tab three.</TabPanel>
  </Tabs>
  ```

## Component props

### Tabs

      { name: 'selectedKey', value: 'string', description: 'Controlled selected tab key' },
      { name: 'defaultSelectedKey', value: 'string', description: 'Default selected tab key' },
      { name: 'onSelectionChange', value: '(key: string) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Tab

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Unique tab identifier (required)' },
      { name: 'href', value: 'string', description: 'Makes the tab a link' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the tab' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Theme Button

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/theme-button.mdx

title: Theme Button

# Theme Button

A button that toggles the page theme between light and dark.

  <ThemeButton variant="outline" />

  ```jsx
  <ThemeButton variant="outline" />
  ```

## Local target

Use the `target` prop to scope theme changes to a specific container instead of globally.

  <ThemeButtonExample />

  ```jsx
  const ref = useRef(null);

  <Box ref={ref}>
    <ThemeButton target={ref} />
  </Box>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'target', value: 'RefObject | HTMLElement', description: 'Element to apply theme to (default: global)' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'ButtonVariant', description: '"default" | "primary" | "outline" | "quiet" (default: "quiet")' },
      { name: 'size', value: 'ButtonSize', description: '"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"' },
      { name: 'onPress', value: '(e: PressEvent) => void', description: 'Called when button is pressed' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

---

# Theme Switcher

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/actions-navigation/theme-switcher.mdx

title: Theme Switcher

# Theme Switcher

A segmented control that allows users to choose between light, dark, or system theme.

  <ThemeSwitcher />

  ```jsx
  <ThemeSwitcher />
  ```

## Features

- Shows all three options (light, dark, system) at once
- Highlights the currently selected option
- Persists the mode preference to localStorage
- Automatically responds to system theme changes when "system" is selected

## Component props

      { name: 'className', value: 'string', description: 'Additional CSS classes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Accordion

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/accordion.mdx

title: Accordion

# Accordion

A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal an associated section of content.

  <Accordion>
    <AccordionItem id="one">
      <div>What is supply and demand?</div>
      <div>
        Supply and demand is an economic model of price determination in a market. It states that
        the price of a good or service is determined by the quantity available (supply) and the
        desire for it (demand).
      </div>
    </AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem id="two">
      <div>What is an algorithm?</div>
      <div>
        An algorithm is a set of well-defined instructions for performing a task or solving a
        problem.
      </div>
    </AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem id="three">
      <div>What is the second law of thermodynamics?</div>
      <div>
        The second law of thermodynamics states that the total entropy of an isolated system can
        never decrease over time, and is often associated with the concept that natural processes
        tend to lead towards a state of greater disorder.
      </div>
    </AccordionItem>
  </Accordion>

  ```jsx
  <Accordion>
    <AccordionItem id="one">
      <div>What is supply and demand?</div>
      <div>
        Supply and demand is an economic model of price determination in a market. It states that
        the price of a good or service is determined by the quantity available (supply) and the
        desire for it (demand).
      </div>
    </AccordionItem>
    <AccordionItem id="two">

      </div>
    </AccordionItem>

  ```

      { name: 'defaultExpandedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Default expanded keys' },

# Calendar

      { name: 'maxValue', value: 'Date', description: 'Maximum selectable date' },

# Data Card

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/data-card.mdx

title: Data Card

# Data Card

A structured display component for presenting key-value pairs in a vertical list format. Useful for profile cards, detail panels, summary views, or any context where labeled data needs clear presentation.

  <DataCard
      { id: 'name', label: 'Name', value: 'Bob' },
      { id: 'title', label: 'Title', value: 'Vice President' },
      { id: 'age', label: 'Age', value: '42' },
  />

  ```jsx
  <DataCard
    data={[
      { id: 'name', label: 'Name', value: 'Bob' },
      { id: 'title', label: 'Title', value: 'Vice President' },
      { id: 'age', label: 'Age', value: '42' },
    ]}
  />
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'data', value: 'object[]', description: 'Array of { label, value } objects' },
      { name: 'labelWidth', value: 'string', description: 'Width of label column (default: "auto")' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Data Table

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/data-table.mdx

title: Data Table

# Data Table

A declarative table component for displaying structured data with minimal configuration. Define columns and pass data to quickly render sortable, formatted tables. Ideal for admin panels, lists, and data-heavy interfaces.

      { id: 1, name: 'Bob', title: 'CEO', email: <a href="#">bob@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 2, name: 'Fred', title: 'VP Marketing', email: <a href="#">fred@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 3, name: 'Ted', title: 'Engineer', email: <a href="#">ted@aol.com</a> },
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />
    <DataColumn id="actions" label="" align="end">
      <MenuTrigger>
        <Button variant="outline" size="xs">
          {`⋯`}
        </Button>
        <Popover>
          <Menu>
            <MenuItem id="email">Send email</MenuItem>
            <MenuItem id="phone">Call phone</MenuItem>
          </Menu>
        </Popover>
      </MenuTrigger>
    </DataColumn>

  ```jsx
  <DataTable data={data}>
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" />
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Name" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />
  </DataTable>
  ```

## Column widths

      { id: 1, name: 'Bob', title: 'CEO', email: <a href="#">bob@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 2, name: 'Fred', title: 'VP Marketing', email: <a href="#">fred@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 3, name: 'Ted', title: 'Engineer', email: <a href="#">ted@aol.com</a> },
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" width="50px" />
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Name" width="2fr" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />
    <DataColumn id="actions" label="" align="end">
      <MenuTrigger>
        <Button variant="outline" size="xs">
          {`⋯`}
        </Button>
        <Popover>
          <Menu>
            <MenuItem id="email">Send email</MenuItem>
            <MenuItem id="phone">Call phone</MenuItem>
          </Menu>
        </Popover>
      </MenuTrigger>
    </DataColumn>

  ```jsx
  <DataTable data={data}>
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" width="50px" />
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Name" width="2fr" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />
  </DataTable>
  ```

## As cards

      { id: 1, name: 'Bob', title: 'CEO', email: <a href="#">bob@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 2, name: 'Fred', title: 'VP Marketing', email: <a href="#">fred@aol.com</a> },
      { id: 3, name: 'Ted', title: 'Engineer', email: <a href="#">ted@aol.com</a> },
    displayMode="cards"
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" width="50px" />
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Name" width="2fr" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />

  ```jsx
  <DataTable data={data} displayMode="cards">
    <DataColumn id="id" label="ID" />
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Name" />
    <DataColumn id="title" label="Title" />
    <DataColumn id="email" label="Email" />
  </DataTable>
  ```

## Component props

### DataTable

      { name: 'data', value: 'object[]', description: 'Array of data objects to display' },
      { name: 'displayMode', value: 'DisplayMode', description: '"table" | "cards"' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### DataColumn

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Column key matching data property (required)' },
      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Column header text' },
      { name: 'width', value: 'string', description: 'Column width (e.g., "100px", "2fr")' },
      { name: 'align', value: 'Alignment', description: '"start" | "center" | "end"' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Icon

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/icon.mdx

title: Icon

# Icon

A wrapper around SVG elements to help control size, color and rotation.

  <Icon>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>

  ```jsx
  <Icon>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  ```

## Sizes

  <Icon size="xs">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="sm">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="xl">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>

  ```jsx
  <Icon size="xs">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="sm">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="xl">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  ```

## Rotation

<Example direction="row">
  <Icon size="md">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={90}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={180}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={270}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>

  ```jsx
  <Icon size="md">
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={90}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={180}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="md" rotate={270}>
    <Lucide.Wifi />
  </Icon>
  ```

## Fill and stroke colors

Control SVG fill and stroke colors using the `fillColor` and `strokeColor` props.

<Example direction="row" gap="4">
  <Icon size="lg" fillColor="blue-500">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg" strokeColor="red-500" strokeWidth="2">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg" fillColor="green-500" strokeColor="green-700" strokeWidth="1">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>

  ```jsx
  <Icon size="lg" fillColor="blue-500">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg" strokeColor="red-500" strokeWidth="2">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>
  <Icon size="lg" fillColor="green-500" strokeColor="green-700" strokeWidth="1">
    <Lucide.Heart />
  </Icon>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'size', value: 'IconSize', description: '"xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" (default: "sm")' },
      { name: 'color', value: 'FontColor', description: 'Icon color' },
      { name: 'rotate', value: 'number', description: 'Rotation in degrees' },
      { name: 'strokeWidth', value: 'StrokeWidth', description: '"0.5" | "1" | "1.5" | "2" | "3" | "4"' },
      { name: 'strokeColor', value: 'StrokeColor', description: 'SVG stroke color (semantic, Tailwind color, or color-shade)' },
      { name: 'fillColor', value: 'FillColor', description: 'SVG fill color (semantic, Tailwind color, or color-shade)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Image

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/image.mdx

title: Image

# Image

An image component with built-in support for responsive sizing, object-fit modes, and border radius. Handles common image display patterns while maintaining aspect ratios and proper scaling.

  <Box maxWidth="480px">
    <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" />
  ```

## Object fit

  <Column gap="4">
    <Label>Cover</Label>
    <Box maxWidth="480px" height="480px" border>
      <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="cover" />
    </Box>
    <Label>Fill</Label>
    <Box maxWidth="480px" height="480px" border>
      <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="fill" />
    </Box>
    <Label>Contain</Label>
    <Box maxWidth="480px" height="480px" border>
      <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="contain" />
    </Box>
    <Label>Scale down</Label>
    <Box maxWidth="480px" height="480px" border>
      <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="scale-down" />
    </Box>
    <Label>None</Label>
    <Box maxWidth="480px" height="480px" border overflow="hidden">
      <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="none" />
    </Box>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="cover" />
  <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="contain" />
  <Image src="/images/sample.jpg" alt="Image" objectFit="fill" />
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'src', value: 'string', description: 'Image source URL (required)' },
      { name: 'alt', value: 'string', description: 'Alternative text' },
      { name: 'objectFit', value: 'ObjectFit', description: '"fill" | "contain" | "cover" | "none" | "scale-down"' },
      { name: 'isCentered', value: 'boolean', description: 'Centers the image horizontally' },
      { name: 'borderRadius', value: 'BorderRadius', description: 'Border radius value' },
      { name: 'shadow', value: 'BoxShadow', description: 'Box shadow value' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# List

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/list.mdx

title: List

# List

A list displays a collection of items and allows a user to select one or more of them.

  <List>
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Four</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Five</ListItem>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List>
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
  </List>
  ```

## Separators

  <List>
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListSeparator />
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Four</ListItem>
    <ListSeparator />
    <ListItem>Five</ListItem>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List>
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListSeparator />
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
  </List>
  ```

## Sections

  <List>
    <ListSection title="Introduction">
      <ListItem>One</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    </ListSection>
    <ListSection title="Summary">
      <ListItem>Four</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Five</ListItem>
    </ListSection>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List>
    <ListSection title="Introduction">
      <ListItem>One</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    </ListSection>
    <ListSection title="Summary">
      <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    </ListSection>
  </List>
  ```

## Single select

  <List selectionMode="single">
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Four</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Five</ListItem>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List selectionMode="single">
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
  </List>
  ```

## Multiple select

  <List selectionMode="multiple">
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Four</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Five</ListItem>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List selectionMode="multiple">
    <ListItem>One</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem>Three</ListItem>
  </List>
  ```

## Preselected

  <List selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['three', 'five']}>
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="four">Four</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="five">Five</ListItem>
  </List>

  ```jsx
  <List selectionMode="multiple" defaultSelectedKeys={['three', 'five']}>
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
  </List>
  ```

## Component props

### List

      { name: 'selectionMode', value: 'SelectionMode', description: '"none" | "single" | "multiple"' },
      { name: 'selectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Controlled selected keys' },
      { name: 'defaultSelectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Default selected keys' },
      { name: 'onSelectionChange', value: '(keys: Selection) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### ListItem

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Unique item identifier' },
      { name: 'textValue', value: 'string', description: 'Text value for accessibility' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the item' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Table

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/table.mdx

title: Table

# Table

A table displays data in rows and columns and enables a user to navigate its contents via
directional navigation keys, and optionally supports row selection and sorting.

  <Table>
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn>Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Email</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Date created</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Bob</TableCell>
        <TableCell>bob@aol.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>5/5/2020</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Fred</TableCell>
        <TableCell>fred@yahoo.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>4/7/2021</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Ted</TableCell>
        <TableCell>ted@gmail.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>11/20/2010</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Joe</TableCell>
        <TableCell>joe@outlook.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>1/18/2016</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>

  ```jsx
  <Table>
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn>Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Email</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Date created</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Bob</TableCell>
        <TableCell>bob@aol.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>5/5/2020</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```

## Selection

  <Table selectionMode="multiple">
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn style={{ maxWidth: 50 }}>
        <Checkbox slot="selection" />
      </TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Email</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Date created</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell style={{ maxWidth: 50 }}>
          <Checkbox slot="selection" />
        </TableCell>
        <TableCell>Bob</TableCell>
        <TableCell>bob@aol.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>5/5/2020</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell style={{ maxWidth: 50 }}>
          <Checkbox slot="selection" />
        </TableCell>
        <TableCell>Fred</TableCell>
        <TableCell>fred@yahoo.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>4/7/2021</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell style={{ maxWidth: 50 }}>
          <Checkbox slot="selection" />
        </TableCell>
        <TableCell>Ted</TableCell>
        <TableCell>ted@gmail.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>11/20/2010</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell style={{ maxWidth: 50 }}>
          <Checkbox slot="selection" />
        </TableCell>
        <TableCell>Joe</TableCell>
        <TableCell>joe@outlook.com</TableCell>
        <TableCell>1/18/2016</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>

  ```jsx
  <Table selectionMode="multiple">
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn><Checkbox slot="selection" /></TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn>Email</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell><Checkbox slot="selection" /></TableCell>
        <TableCell>Bob</TableCell>
        <TableCell>bob@aol.com</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```

## Alignment

  <Table>
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn align="start">Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn align="center">Type</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn align="end">Date modified</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell align="start">Games</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="center">File folder</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="end">6/7/2020</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell align="start">Program Files</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="center">File folder</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="end">4/7/2021</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>

  ```jsx
  <Table>
    <TableHeader>
      <TableColumn align="start">Name</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn align="center">Type</TableColumn>
      <TableColumn align="end">Date</TableColumn>
    </TableHeader>
    <TableBody>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell align="start">Games</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="center">Folder</TableCell>
        <TableCell align="end">6/7/2020</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </TableBody>
  </Table>
  ```

## Component props

### Table

      { name: 'selectionMode', value: 'SelectionMode', description: '"none" | "single" | "multiple"' },
      { name: 'selectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Controlled selected row keys' },
      { name: 'defaultSelectedKeys', value: 'string[]', description: 'Default selected row keys' },
      { name: 'onSelectionChange', value: '(keys: Selection) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### TableColumn / TableCell

      { name: 'align', value: 'Alignment', description: '"start" | "center" | "end"' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Tag Group

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/data-display/tag-group.mdx

title: Tag Group

# Tag Group

A tag group displays a collection of tags that can optionally be removed.

  <TagGroup label="Categories">
    <Tag id="react">React</Tag>
    <Tag id="vue">Vue</Tag>
    <Tag id="angular">Angular</Tag>
  </TagGroup>

  ```jsx
  <TagGroup label="Categories">
    <Tag id="react">React</Tag>
    <Tag id="vue">Vue</Tag>
    <Tag id="angular">Angular</Tag>
  </TagGroup>
  ```

## Removable

Add `onRemove` to make tags removable. An X button will appear on each tag.

  <RemovableTagGroupExample />

  ```jsx
  <TagGroup label="Skills" onRemove={keys => console.log('Remove:', [...keys])}>
    <Tag id="javascript">JavaScript</Tag>
    <Tag id="typescript">TypeScript</Tag>
    <Tag id="python">Python</Tag>
  </TagGroup>
  ```

## Variants

  <Column gap="3">
    <TagGroup label="Default">
      <Tag id="one">Default</Tag>
      <Tag id="two">Tags</Tag>
    </TagGroup>
    <TagGroup label="Outline">
      <Tag id="one" variant="outline">Outline</Tag>
      <Tag id="two" variant="outline">Tags</Tag>
    </TagGroup>
    <TagGroup label="Primary">
      <Tag id="one" variant="primary">Primary</Tag>
      <Tag id="two" variant="primary">Tags</Tag>
    </TagGroup>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <TagGroup label="Default">
    <Tag id="one">Default</Tag>
    <Tag id="two">Tags</Tag>
  </TagGroup>

  <TagGroup label="Outline">
    <Tag id="one" variant="outline">Outline</Tag>
    <Tag id="two" variant="outline">Tags</Tag>
  </TagGroup>

  <TagGroup label="Primary">
    <Tag id="one" variant="primary">Primary</Tag>
    <Tag id="two" variant="primary">Tags</Tag>
  </TagGroup>
  ```

## Component props

### TagGroup

      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Label text displayed above the group' },
      { name: 'onRemove', value: '(keys: Set<Key>) => void', description: 'Called when tags are removed. Enables remove buttons.' },
      { name: 'disabledKeys', value: 'Iterable<Key>', description: 'Keys of tags that cannot be removed' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Tag

      { name: 'id', value: 'string', description: 'Unique tag identifier (required)' },
      { name: 'variant', value: '"default" | "outline" | "primary"', description: 'Visual style variant' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the tag' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Breakpoints

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/design/breakpoints.mdx

title: Breakpoints

# Breakpoints

Breakpoints allow you to build responsive layouts by reacting to screen size changes.
Zen uses Tailwind's default breakpoints with a **mobile-first** approach. Styles are applied
from the smallest screen up, and breakpoints specify the **minimum width** at which styles take effect.

      { name: 'base', device: 'All devices', width: '0px' },
      { name: 'sm', device: 'Small devices', width: '640px' },
      { name: 'md', device: 'Medium devices', width: '768px' },
      { name: 'lg', device: 'Large devices', width: '1024px' },
      { name: 'xl', device: 'Extra large devices', width: '1280px' },
      { name: '2xl', device: 'Extra extra large devices', width: '1536px' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Breakpoint" />
    <DataColumn id="device" label="Device" />
    <DataColumn id="width" label="Min Width" />

## Usage

Certain properties of layout components accept a `Responsive` object, which specifies what value
to apply at a given breakpoint. Use `'base'` for the mobile-first value that applies to all screen sizes.

For example, the [Heading](/docs/typography/heading) component takes a `size` prop. If we pass in a
`Responsive` object, we can specify which sizes to display at different breakpoints.

  <Heading
    size={{
      base: 'lg',
      sm: 'xl',
      md: '2xl',
      lg: '3xl',
      xl: '4xl',
    }}
    {`This text will shrink/grow as the screen resizes.`}
  </Heading>

```jsx
<Heading
  size={{
    base: 'lg',    // Base size for all screens
    sm: 'xl',      // 640px and up
    md: '2xl',     // 768px and up
    lg: '3xl',     // 1024px and up
    xl: '4xl',     // 1280px and up
  }}
>
  This text will shrink/grow as the screen resizes.
</Heading>
```

## useBreakpoint Hook

The `useBreakpoint` hook returns the current breakpoint based on screen width.

```jsx
import { useBreakpoint } from '@umami/react-zen';

function MyComponent() {
  const breakpoint = useBreakpoint();

  // breakpoint will be: 'base' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | '2xl'
  return <Text>Current breakpoint: {breakpoint}</Text>;
}
```

  <BreakpointExample />

---

# Colors

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/design/colors.mdx

title: Colors

# Colors

Our color system is based on Tailwind CSS colors. There are two categories of colors: semantic colors and accent colors.

## Semantic colors

Semantic colors provide meaning to UI elements and are used for common states.

<Example direction="row" gap="6">
  <Column alignItems="center">
    <ExampleBox backgroundColor="primary" />
    <Text align="center">primary</Text>
  </Column>
  <Column alignItems="center">
    <ExampleBox backgroundColor="muted" />
    <Text align="center">muted</Text>
  </Column>
  <Column alignItems="center">
    <ExampleBox backgroundColor="transparent" />
    <Text align="center">transparent</Text>
  </Column>

## Accent colors

Accent colors provide additional meaning to UI elements and are used in buttons, links and statuses.

<Example direction="row" wrap="wrap">
  <AccentColorsExample />

## Text colors

<Example direction="row" gap="4">
  <Text color="primary">Primary text</Text>
  <Text color="muted">Muted text</Text>
  <Text color="disabled">Disabled text</Text>
  <Text color="red">Colored text</Text>

  ```jsx
  <Text color="primary">Primary text</Text>
  <Text color="muted">Muted text</Text>
  <Text color="disabled">Disabled text</Text>
  <Text color="red">Colored text</Text>
  ```

## Color shades

You can use any Tailwind color with a specific shade (50-950). If no shade is specified, 500 is used by default.

<Example direction="row" gap="4">
  <Text color="blue-300">blue-300</Text>
  <Text color="blue-500">blue-500</Text>
  <Text color="blue-700">blue-700</Text>
  <Text color="blue-900">blue-900</Text>

  ```jsx
  <Text color="blue-300">blue-300</Text>
  <Text color="blue-500">blue-500</Text>
  <Text color="blue-700">blue-700</Text>
  <Text color="blue-900">blue-900</Text>
  ```

## Icon colors

Icons support the same color props including shades.

<Example direction="row" gap="4">
  <Icon color="green-400" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="blue-500" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="purple-600" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="red-700" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>

  ```jsx
  <Icon color="green-400" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="blue-500" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="purple-600" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  <Icon color="red-700" size="lg"><Lucide.Wifi /></Icon>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'color', value: 'FontColor', description: 'SemanticColor | ColorName | TailwindColor' },
      { name: 'backgroundColor', value: 'BackgroundColor', description: 'SemanticColor | SurfaceColor | ColorName | TailwindColor' },
      { name: 'borderColor', value: 'BorderColor', description: 'SemanticColor | ColorName | TailwindColor' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

Where `ColorName` is a base Tailwind color (e.g., `blue`, `red`) and `TailwindColor` is a color with shade (e.g., `blue-500`, `red-300`).

## Available colors

The following Tailwind colors are available, each with shades from 50 to 950:

  <ColorSwatchesExample />

# Customization

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/design/customization.mdx

title: Customization

# Customization

Zen uses CSS custom properties (variables) for all design tokens, making it easy to customize the look and feel of your application. You can override these variables to match your brand or create entirely custom themes.

## Overriding variables

To customize Zen, override the CSS variables in your stylesheet. Variables defined on `:root` apply globally, while scoped selectors can target specific themes.

```css
:root {
  /* Override for both light and dark themes */
  --font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
}

/* Override only in light mode */
[data-theme="light"] {
  --surface-base: #fafafa;
  --text-primary: #1a1a1a;
}

/* Override only in dark mode */
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --surface-base: #0a0a0a;
  --text-primary: #fafafa;
}
```

## Creating a branded theme

Here's an example of creating a custom branded theme with a blue accent:

```css
[data-theme="light"] {
  /* Primary button and accent color */
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.2 250);
  --primary-foreground: #ffffff;
  --focus-ring: oklch(0.7 0.15 250);
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  /* Lighter primary for dark mode */
  --primary: oklch(0.7 0.15 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.2 0 0);
  --focus-ring: var(--primary);
}
```

## CSS variable reference

### Primary

The primary accent color used for primary buttons and branded elements.

      { variable: '--primary', description: 'Primary/brand accent color (button backgrounds)' },
      { variable: '--primary-foreground', description: 'Text color on primary backgrounds' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Surfaces

Background colors for different elevation levels.

      { variable: '--surface-base', description: 'Primary background (page level)' },
      { variable: '--surface-raised', description: 'Elevated surfaces (cards, modals)' },
      { variable: '--surface-sunken', description: 'Recessed areas (inputs, wells)' },
      { variable: '--surface-overlay', description: 'Overlays (dropdowns, popovers)' },
      { variable: '--surface-inverted', description: 'Inverted background (tooltips)' },
      { variable: '--surface-disabled', description: 'Disabled element background' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Text

Text colors for different emphasis levels.

      { variable: '--text-primary', description: 'Primary text (headings, body)' },
      { variable: '--text-muted', description: 'Muted text (labels, placeholders, hints)' },
      { variable: '--text-disabled', description: 'Disabled text' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Borders

Border colors for different emphasis levels.

      { variable: '--border-default', description: 'Default border (inputs, cards)' },
      { variable: '--border-muted', description: 'Subtle borders (dividers)' },
      { variable: '--border-strong', description: 'Emphasized borders (focus, active)' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Interactive states

Colors for interactive elements like buttons, checkboxes, and list items.

      { variable: '--interactive-bg', description: 'Default interactive background' },
      { variable: '--interactive-bg-hover', description: 'Hover state background' },
      { variable: '--interactive-bg-pressed', description: 'Pressed/active state background' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Focus

Focus ring styles for accessibility.

      { variable: '--focus-ring', description: 'Focus ring color' },
      { variable: '--focus-ring-offset', description: 'Focus ring offset color (gap)' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Status colors

Colors for feedback states (info, success, warning, error).

      { variable: '--status-info', description: 'Info accent color' },
      { variable: '--status-info-bg', description: 'Info background' },
      { variable: '--status-info-text', description: 'Info text color' },
      { variable: '--status-success', description: 'Success accent color' },
      { variable: '--status-success-bg', description: 'Success background' },
      { variable: '--status-success-text', description: 'Success text color' },
      { variable: '--status-warning', description: 'Warning accent color' },
      { variable: '--status-warning-bg', description: 'Warning background' },
      { variable: '--status-warning-text', description: 'Warning text color' },
      { variable: '--status-error', description: 'Error accent color' },
      { variable: '--status-error-bg', description: 'Error background' },
      { variable: '--status-error-text', description: 'Error text color' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Typography

Font family variables.

      { variable: '--font-family', description: 'Default font stack' },
      { variable: '--font-family-mono', description: 'Monospace font stack' },
    <DataColumn id="variable" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

## Using OKLCH colors

Zen uses OKLCH color values for better color manipulation and perceptual uniformity. OKLCH colors are defined as `oklch(lightness chroma hue)`:

- **Lightness**: 0 (black) to 1 (white)
- **Chroma**: 0 (gray) to ~0.4 (vivid)
- **Hue**: 0-360 degrees (color wheel)

```css
:root {
  /* A vibrant blue */
  --brand-color: oklch(0.6 0.2 250);

  /* A muted green */
  --subtle-green: oklch(0.7 0.1 150);

  /* With transparency */
  --overlay-bg: oklch(0.2 0 0 / 0.5);
}
```

## Tips

- Always provide both light and dark theme overrides for a consistent experience
- Use OKLCH for colors to maintain perceptual consistency across themes
- Test your customizations in both themes to ensure adequate contrast
- Use browser DevTools to inspect and experiment with CSS variables in real-time

# Fonts

title: Fonts

# Fonts

The default fonts we use are [Inter](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inter) for regular text and
[JetBrains Mono](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/JetBrains+Mono) for monospace text.

## Font sizes

Font sizes use Tailwind's naming convention.

    <Text size="xs">xs</Text>
    <Text size="sm">sm</Text>
    <Text size="base">base</Text>
    <Text size="lg">lg</Text>
    <Text size="xl">xl</Text>

    <Text size="5xl">5xl</Text>
    <Text size="6xl">6xl</Text>
    <Text size="7xl">7xl</Text>
    <Text size="8xl">8xl</Text>
    <Text size="9xl">9xl</Text>

  ```jsx
  <Text size="xs">xs</Text>
  <Text size="sm">sm</Text>
  <Text size="base">base</Text>
  <Text size="lg">lg</Text>
  <Text size="xl">xl</Text>
  <Text size="2xl">2xl</Text>
  ```

      { name: 'xs', value: '12px' },

      { name: '4xl', value: '36px' },
      { name: '5xl', value: '48px' },

      { name: '7xl', value: '72px' },
      { name: '8xl', value: '96px' },
      { name: '9xl', value: '128px' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Value" />
    <DataColumn id="value" label="Size" />

## Font weights

    <Text weight="thin">Thin (100)</Text>
    <Text weight="extralight">Extra Light (200)</Text>

      { name: 'thin', value: '100' },

    <DataColumn id="name" label="Value" />
    <DataColumn id="value" label="Weight" />

## Usage in typography components

Font properties are used by typography components to control text appearance. [Text](/docs/typography/text) is the primary component for rendering text and accepts all font-related props. [Heading](/docs/typography/heading) uses a subset of larger sizes appropriate for headings.

- **size** - Controls the font size. Text defaults to `base`, while Heading sizes map to appropriate heading levels.
- **weight** - Controls the font weight. Text defaults to `normal`, Heading defaults to `semibold`.

All font props accept responsive values for adapting typography across breakpoints.

## Component props

      { name: 'size', value: 'Responsive<FontSize>', description: '"xs" | "sm" | "base" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | ... | "9xl"' },
      { name: 'weight', value: 'Responsive<FontWeight>', description: '"thin" | "extralight" | "light" | "normal" | "medium" | "semibold" | "bold" | "extrabold" | "black"' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

# Spacing

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/design/spacing.mdx

title: Spacing

# Spacing

Spacing defines values that are used in `margin`, `padding` and `gap` properties. The spacing scale uses Tailwind's native values.

  <Column gap="6">
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Padding</Label>
      <Box border padding="4" borderRadius>
        <Text>Box with padding="4"</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Margin</Label>
      <Box border borderRadius>
        <Box backgroundColor="primary" padding="2" margin="4">
          <Text color="primary">Box with margin="4"</Text>
        </Box>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Gap</Label>
      <Row gap="4">
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Column gap="6">
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Padding</Label>
      <Box border padding="4" borderRadius>
        <Text>Box with padding="4"</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Margin</Label>
      <Box border borderRadius>
        <Box backgroundColor="primary" padding="2" margin="4">
          <Text color="primary">Box with margin="4"</Text>
        </Box>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Gap</Label>
      <Row gap="4">
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Column>
  ```

## Spacing values

      { name: '0', value: '0px' },
      { name: 'px', value: '1px' },
      { name: '0.5', value: '2px' },
      { name: '1', value: '4px' },
      { name: '1.5', value: '6px' },
      { name: '2', value: '8px' },
      { name: '2.5', value: '10px' },
      { name: '3', value: '12px' },
      { name: '3.5', value: '14px' },
      { name: '4', value: '16px' },
      { name: '5', value: '20px' },
      { name: '6', value: '24px' },
      { name: '7', value: '28px' },
      { name: '8', value: '32px' },
      { name: '9', value: '36px' },
      { name: '10', value: '40px' },
      { name: '11', value: '44px' },
      { name: '12', value: '48px' },
      { name: '14', value: '56px' },
      { name: '16', value: '64px' },
      { name: '20', value: '80px' },
      { name: '24', value: '96px' },
      { name: '28', value: '112px' },
      { name: '32', value: '128px' },

      { name: '44', value: '176px' },

      { name: '96', value: '384px' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Value" />
    <DataColumn id="value" label="Size" />

## Usage in layout components

Spacing values are used throughout the layout system. [Box](/docs/layout/box) and all components that extend it ([Row](/docs/layout/row), [Column](/docs/layout/column), [Grid](/docs/layout/grid), [Flexbox](/docs/layout/flexbox)) accept spacing props for controlling internal and external space.

- **padding** - Controls internal space within an element. Use directional variants (`paddingX`, `paddingY`, `paddingTop`, etc.) for more control.
- **margin** - Controls external space around an element. Supports negative values for overlapping layouts.
- **gap** - Controls space between child elements in flex and grid containers.

All spacing props accept responsive values for adapting layouts across breakpoints.

## Component props

      { name: 'padding', value: 'Responsive<Padding>', description: 'true | Spacing' },
      { name: 'margin', value: 'Responsive<Spacing>', description: 'Spacing (supports negative values)' },
      { name: 'gap', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

# Themes

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/design/themes.mdx

title: Themes

# Themes

Zen supports light and dark themes out of the box. Themes are applied using CSS custom properties that automatically adjust colors, backgrounds, and borders based on the active theme.

## Setup

Wrap your application with `ZenProvider` to enable theme support.

```jsx
import { ZenProvider } from '@umami/react-zen';

function App() {
  return (
    <ZenProvider>
      <YourApp />
    </ZenProvider>
  );
}
```

## Theme options

You can configure the initial theme using the `theme` or `colorScheme` props.

```jsx
// Force a specific theme
<ZenProvider theme="dark">

// Use system preference
<ZenProvider colorScheme="system">

// Default to light, but respect system preference
<ZenProvider colorScheme="light">
```

## ThemeButton

Use the `ThemeButton` component to let users toggle between light and dark themes.

  <ThemeButton variant="outline" />

```jsx
<ThemeButton variant="outline" />
```

## Local themes

You can scope theme changes to a specific container using the `target` prop. This allows parts of your UI to have a different theme than the rest of the page.

  <ThemeButtonExample />

```jsx
function LocalThemeExample() {
  const containerRef = useRef(null);

  return (
    <Box ref={containerRef} padding="6" backgroundColor="surface-base">
      <Row alignItems="center" justifyContent="space-between">
        <Text>This container has its own theme</Text>
        <ThemeButton target={containerRef} />
      </Row>
    </Box>
  );
}
```

## useTheme hook

Access and control the current theme programmatically with the `useTheme` hook.

```jsx
import { useTheme } from '@umami/react-zen';

function MyComponent() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();

  return (
    <Button onPress={() => setTheme(theme === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light')}>
      Current theme: {theme}
    </Button>
  );
}
```

## CSS variables

Themes work by redefining CSS custom properties. The following variables change based on the active theme:

      { name: '--surface-base', description: 'Primary background color' },
      { name: '--surface-raised', description: 'Elevated surface background' },
      { name: '--surface-sunken', description: 'Recessed surface background' },
      { name: '--surface-overlay', description: 'Overlay/modal background' },
      { name: '--text-primary', description: 'Primary text color' },
      { name: '--text-muted', description: 'Muted/subtle text color' },
      { name: '--border-default', description: 'Default border color' },
      { name: '--border-strong', description: 'Emphasized border color' },
      { name: '--interactive-bg', description: 'Interactive element background' },
      { name: '--primary', description: 'Primary/accent color' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Variable" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

## Theme persistence

Theme preference is automatically saved to `localStorage` under the key `theme`. When the page loads, the stored preference is restored.

## Dark mode classes

Zen applies both `data-theme="dark"` attribute and the `.dark` class to the root element for maximum compatibility with Tailwind CSS and other frameworks.

## Color palettes

Zen supports multiple gray-scale palettes inspired by Tailwind CSS. Each palette has a different color temperature and character.

  <PaletteSwatchesExample />

### Available palettes

      { name: 'neutral', description: 'Pure gray with no color tint (default)' },
      { name: 'slate', description: 'Cool blue-gray tones' },
      { name: 'gray', description: 'Slight blue tint' },
      { name: 'zinc', description: 'Subtle blue undertones' },
      { name: 'stone', description: 'Warm tan/brown tones' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Palette" />
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### Setting the palette

You can set the palette via `ZenProvider` or programmatically with `useTheme`.

```jsx
// Via provider
<ZenProvider palette="slate">
  <YourApp />
</ZenProvider>

// Programmatically
const { palette, setPalette } = useTheme();
setPalette('zinc');
```

### PaletteSwitcher

Use the `PaletteSwitcher` component to let users switch between palettes.

```jsx
<PaletteSwitcher />
```

### Palette persistence

Palette preference is automatically saved to `localStorage` under the key `zen.palette`. The `data-palette` attribute is applied to the root element.

# Alert Banner

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/feedback-status/alert-banner.mdx

title: Alert Banner

# Alert Banner

Alert banners show pressing and high-signal messages, such as system alerts.
They're meant to be noticed and prompt users to take action.

  <AlertBanner
    title="New update available!"
    description="Version 2.0 has been released."
    icon={<Lucide.Rocket />}
    <Button variant="outline">Dismiss</Button>
    <Button variant="primary">Download</Button>
  </AlertBanner>

  ```jsx
  <AlertBanner
    title="New update available!"
    description="Version 2.0 has been released."
    icon={<Lucide.Rocket />}
  >
    <Button>Dismiss</Button>
    <Button variant="primary">Download</Button>
  </AlertBanner>
  ```

## Variants

<Example direction="column">
  <AlertBanner
    variant="info"
    title="Info"
    description="Your free trial will expire in 3 days."
  />
  <AlertBanner
    variant="success"
    title="Success"
    description="Your changes have been saved."
  />
  <AlertBanner
    variant="warning"
    title="Warning"
    description="Your session is about to expire."
  />
  <AlertBanner
    variant="error"
    title="Error"
    description="The application encountered an error."
  />

  ```jsx
  <AlertBanner variant="info" title="Info" description="Your free trial will expire in 3 days." />
  <AlertBanner variant="success" title="Success" description="Your changes have been saved." />
  <AlertBanner variant="warning" title="Warning" description="Your session is about to expire." />
  <AlertBanner variant="error" title="Error" description="The application encountered an error." />
  ```

## With close button

<Example direction="column">
  <AlertBanner
    variant="info"
    title="Dismissible alert"
    description="Click the X to close this alert."
    allowClose
  />

  ```jsx
  <AlertBanner
    variant="info"
    title="Dismissible alert"
    description="Click the X to close this alert."
    allowClose
    onClose={() => setVisible(false)}
  />
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'title', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Banner title' },
      { name: 'description', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Banner description text' },
      { name: 'icon', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Custom icon (overrides variant icon)' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'AlertVariant', description: '"info" | "success" | "warning" | "error" (default: "info")' },
      { name: 'align', value: 'Alignment', description: '"start" | "center" | "end"' },
      { name: 'allowClose', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows a close button' },
      { name: 'onClose', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when close button is clicked' },
      { name: 'children', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Action buttons or other content' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Alert Dialog

Alert dialogs are a specific type of Dialog. They display important information that users need
to acknowledge.

  <AlertDialogExample />

  ```jsx
  <DialogTrigger>
    <Button variant="primary">Delete account</Button>
    <Modal>
      <AlertDialog title="Are you sure you want to delete your account?">
        <Text>This cannot be undone. All your data will be permanantly deleted.</Text>
      </AlertDialog>
    </Modal>
  </DialogTrigger>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'title', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Dialog title' },
      { name: 'description', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Dialog description' },
      { name: 'isDanger', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows confirm button as danger variant' },
      { name: 'isConfirmDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the confirm button' },
      { name: 'confirmLabel', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Confirm button text (default: "Confirm")' },
      { name: 'cancelLabel', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Cancel button text (default: "Cancel")' },
      { name: 'onConfirm', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when confirm is clicked' },
      { name: 'onCancel', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when cancel is clicked' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Confirmation Dialog

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/feedback-status/confirmation-dialog.mdx

title: Confirmation Dialog

# Confirmation Dialog

A high-friction dialog for destructive or irreversible actions. Requires users to type a confirmation phrase before proceeding, preventing accidental deletions or critical changes.

  <ConfirmationDialogExample />

  ```jsx
  <DialogTrigger>
    <Button variant="danger">Delete account</Button>
    <Modal>
      <ConfirmationDialog
        title="Delete account"
        value={'abc123'}
        confirmLabel="Delete"
        isDanger={true}
      >
        <Text>This cannot be undone. All your data will be permananently deleted.</Text>
      </ConfirmationDialog>
    </Modal>
  </DialogTrigger>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'value', value: 'string', description: 'Text the user must type to confirm (required)' },
      { name: 'confirmMessage', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Message shown above the confirmation input' },
      { name: 'title', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Dialog title' },
      { name: 'isDanger', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows confirm button as danger variant' },
      { name: 'confirmLabel', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Confirm button text' },
      { name: 'cancelLabel', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Cancel button text' },
      { name: 'onConfirm', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when confirmed' },
      { name: 'onCancel', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when cancelled' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Dialog

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/feedback-status/dialog.mdx

title: Dialog

# Dialog

A dialog is an overlay shown above other content in an application.

  <DialogExample />

  ```jsx
  <DialogTrigger>
    <Button variant="primary">Click me</Button>
    <Modal>
      <Dialog title="Sign up for newsletter">
        {({ close }) => {
          return (
            <Form>
              <FormField name="name" label="Name">
                <TextField />
              </FormField>
              <FormField name="email" label="Email">
                <TextField />
              </FormField>
              <FormButtons>
                <Button onPress={close}>Cancel</Button>
                <Button variant="primary" onPress={close}>
                  Sign up
                </Button>
              </FormButtons>
            </Form>
          );
        }}
      </Dialog>
    </Modal>
  </DialogTrigger>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'title', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Dialog title displayed at the top' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'DialogVariant', description: '"sheet" - Full-width variant for side panels' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

      </Dialog>

        </Flexbox>

        </Flexbox>
      </Dialog>
    </Modal>

        <Flexbox justifyContent="center" alignItems="center" paddingX="9" paddingY="8">

          <Switch>Mute</Switch>
        </Column>
      </Dialog>
    </Popover>
  </DialogTrigger>

# Toast

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/feedback-status/toast.mdx

title: Toast

# Toast

A succinct message that is displayed temporarily.

  <ToastExample />

  ```jsx
  <Button onPress={() => toast('Your message has been sent.')}>Show toast</Button>
  ```

## With title

  <ToastTitleExample />

  ```jsx
  <Button
    onPress={() =>
      toast('The application encountered an error.', { title: 'Oops! Something went wrong.' })
    }
  >
    Show toast
  </Button>
  ```

## With action

  <ToastActionExample />

  ```jsx
  <Button
    onPress={() =>
      toast('The task was deleted successfully.', {
        title: 'Task deleted',
        actions: ['Undo'],
      })
    }
  >
    Show toast
  </Button>
  ```

## Variants

  <ToastVariantsExample />

  ```jsx
  <>
    <Button onPress={() => toast('Your message was sent.', { variant: 'success' })}>
      Success toast
    </Button>
    <Button onPress={() => toast('Something went wrong.', { variant: 'error' })}>
      Error toast
    </Button>
  </>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'message', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Toast message content' },
      { name: 'title', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Optional toast title' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'ToastVariant', description: '"default" | "success" | "error"' },
      { name: 'action', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Action element (e.g., button)' },
      { name: 'onAction', value: '() => void', description: 'Called when action is clicked' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />
