# Tooltip

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/feedback-status/tooltip.mdx

title: Tooltip

# Tooltip

A tooltip displays a description of an element on hover or focus.

  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Hover me</Button>
    <Tooltip>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>

  ```jsx
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Hover me</Button>
    <Tooltip>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  ```

## Placement

  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Top</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="top">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Left</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="left">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Right</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="right">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Bottom</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="bottom">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>

  ```jsx
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Top</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="top">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Left</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="left">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Right</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="right">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Bottom</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="bottom">Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  ```

## With arrow

  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Top</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="top" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Left</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="left" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Right</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="right" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Bottom</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="bottom" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>

  ```jsx
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Top</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="top" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Left</Button>

  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipTrigger delay={0}>
    <Button variant="secondary">Bottom</Button>
    <Tooltip placement="bottom" showArrow>Hello</Tooltip>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  ```

## Floating

  <FloatingTooltipExample />

  ```jsx

  </FloatingTooltip>
  ```

      { name: 'placement', value: 'Placement', description: '"top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"' },
      { name: 'showArrow', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows an arrow pointing to the trigger' },
      { name: 'offset', value: 'number', description: 'Distance from the trigger element' },

    <ListItem id="six">Six</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="seven">Seven</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="eight">Eight</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="nine">Nine</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="ten">Ten</ListItem>
  </ComboBox>

  ```jsx
  <ComboBox>
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="four">Four</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="five">Five</ListItem>
  </ComboBox>
  ```

    <Radio value="two">Two</Radio>
    <Radio value="three">Three</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>

    <Radio value="two">Two</Radio>

  </RadioGroup>

  <Box width="300px">
    <Select placeholder="Please select an option">
      <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="four">Four</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="five">Five</ListItem>
    </Select>
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Select placeholder="Please select an option">
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
  </Select>
  ```

## With label

  <Box width="300px">
    <Select label="Select" placeholder="Please select an option">
      <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="four">Four</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="five">Five</ListItem>
    </Select>
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Select label="Select" placeholder="Please select an option">
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
  </Select>
  ```

## With search

  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectSearchExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectSearchExample />
  </Box>
  ```

## Loading

  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectSearchExample isLoading={true} />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectSearchExample isLoading={true} />
  </Box>
  ```

## Custom display

  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectValueExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box width="300px">
    <SelectValueExample />
  </Box>
  ```

## Scrollable

  <Box width="300px">
    <Select maxHeight="300px" placeholder="Please select an option">
      {Array.from(Array(42).keys()).map(i => (
        <ListItem key={i} id={String(i)}>{i}</ListItem>
      ))}
    </Select>
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Select maxHeight="300px" placeholder="Please select an option">
    {Array.from(Array(42).keys()).map(i => (
      <ListItem key={i} id={String(i)}>{i}</ListItem>
    ))}
  </Select>
  ```

## Fullscreen mode

  <Box width="300px">
    <Select label="Select" placeholder="Please select an option" isFullscreen>
      <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="four">Four</ListItem>
      <ListItem id="five">Five</ListItem>
    </Select>
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Select label="Select" placeholder="Please select an option" isFullscreen>
    <ListItem id="one">One</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="two">Two</ListItem>
    <ListItem id="three">Three</ListItem>
  </Select>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'value', value: 'string | number', description: 'Controlled selected value' },
      { name: 'defaultValue', value: 'string | number', description: 'Default selected value' },
      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Label text displayed above the select' },
      { name: 'placeholder', value: 'string', description: 'Placeholder text when no selection' },
      { name: 'isLoading', value: 'boolean', description: 'Shows loading indicator' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Disables the select' },
      { name: 'isFullscreen', value: 'boolean', description: 'Opens options in fullscreen mode' },
      { name: 'allowSearch', value: 'boolean', description: 'Enables search within options' },
      { name: 'searchValue', value: 'string', description: 'Controlled search field value' },
      { name: 'searchDelay', value: 'number', description: 'Debounce delay for search' },
      { name: 'maxHeight', value: 'string | number', description: 'Max height of the dropdown list' },
      { name: 'showIcon', value: 'boolean', description: 'Show chevron icon on trigger button (default: true)' },
      { name: 'onChange', value: '(value: any) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },
      { name: 'onSearch', value: '(value: string) => void', description: 'Called when search value changes' },
      { name: 'renderValue', value: 'ReactNode | Function', description: 'Custom render for selected value' },
      { name: 'buttonProps', value: 'ButtonProps', description: 'Props passed to the trigger button' },
      { name: 'listProps', value: 'ListProps', description: 'Props passed to the list component' },
      { name: 'popoverProps', value: 'PopoverProps', description: 'Props passed to the popover' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Toggle Group

A set of two-state buttons that can be toggled on or off.

  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="single">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>

  ```jsx
  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="single">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```

## Multiple select

  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="multiple">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>

  ```jsx
  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="multiple">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```

## Icons

  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="single">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignLeft />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignCenter />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignRight />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>

  ```jsx
  <ToggleGroup selectionMode="single">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignLeft />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignCenter />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">
      <Icon size="sm">
        <Lucide.AlignRight />
      </Icon>
    </ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```

## Variants

  <Label>Primary</Label>
  <ToggleGroup variant="primary">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>

  ```jsx
  <ToggleGroup variant="primary">
    <ToggleGroupItem id="one">One</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="two">Two</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem id="three">Three</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
  ```

      { name: 'value', value: 'string[]', description: 'Controlled selected values' },
      { name: 'defaultValue', value: 'string[]', description: 'Default selected values' },
      { name: 'variant', value: 'ToggleGroupVariant', description: '"primary"' },
      { name: 'onChange', value: '(value: string[]) => void', description: 'Called when selection changes' },

title: Forms

# Forms

Zen provides a complete form system built on [react-hook-form](https://react-hook-form.com/). The `Form` and `FormField` components handle validation, error display, and field state management with minimal boilerplate.

## How it works

The form system consists of several components that work together:

- **Form** - Wraps your form and provides react-hook-form context
- **FormField** - Connects any input component to the form with automatic value binding and validation
- **FormButtons** - Container for form action buttons
- **FormSubmitButton** - Submit button with automatic loading and disabled states
- **FormResetButton** - Reset button that clears the form to default values

## Basic usage

Wrap your inputs with `FormField` components inside a `Form`. Each `FormField` needs a `name` that corresponds to a key in your form data.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  import { Form, FormField, FormButtons, FormSubmitButton, FormResetButton } from '@umami/react-zen';

  function LoginForm() {
    const handleSubmit = (data) => {
      console.log(data); // { username: '...', password: '...' }
    };

    return (
      <Form
        defaultValues={{ username: '', password: '' }}
        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
      >
        <FormField name="username" label="Username">
          <TextField />
        </FormField>
        <FormField name="password" label="Password">
          <PasswordField />
        </FormField>
        <FormButtons>
          <FormResetButton>Reset</FormResetButton>
          <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Login</FormSubmitButton>
        </FormButtons>
      </Form>
    );
  }
  ```

## Validation

Add validation rules to `FormField` using the `rules` prop. This uses react-hook-form's validation API.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormValidationExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
    <FormField
      name="email"
      label="Email"
      rules={{
        required: 'Email is required',
        pattern: {
          value: /^[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}$/i,
          message: 'Invalid email address',
        },
      }}
    >
      <TextField />
    </FormField>
    <FormField
      name="age"
      label="Age"
      rules={{
        required: 'Age is required',
        validate: (value) => {
          const num = parseInt(value, 10);
          if (isNaN(num)) return 'Must be a number';
          if (num < 18) return 'Must be 18 or older';
          return true;
        },
      }}
    >
      <TextField />
    </FormField>
    <FormButtons>
      <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
    </FormButtons>
  </Form>
  ```

### Common validation rules

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `required` | Field must have a value |
| `min` | Minimum value for numbers |
| `max` | Maximum value for numbers |
| `minLength` | Minimum string length |
| `maxLength` | Maximum string length |
| `pattern` | Regex pattern to match |
| `validate` | Custom validation function |

## Loading states

`FormSubmitButton` automatically shows a loading spinner and disables itself while the form is submitting. This happens when your `onSubmit` handler returns a Promise.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormLoadingExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Form
    defaultValues={{ name: '' }}
    onSubmit={async (data) => {
      // Simulate API call
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
      console.log('Submitted:', data);
    }}
  >
    <FormField name="name" label="Name" rules={{ required: 'Name is required' }}>
      <TextField />
    </FormField>
    <FormButtons>
      <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Save</FormSubmitButton>
    </FormButtons>
  </Form>
  ```

The submit button is automatically disabled when:
- The form has not been modified (`isDirty` is false)
- The form has validation errors (`isValid` is false)
- The form is currently submitting (`isSubmitting` is true)

You can override this behavior with the `isDisabled` prop.

## Error handling

Pass an `error` prop to `Form` to display an error banner above the form. This is useful for showing server-side validation errors or API failures.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormErrorExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  function MyForm() {
    const [error, setError] = useState(null);

    const handleSubmit = async (data) => {
      try {
        await api.submit(data);
      } catch (err) {
        setError(err.message);
      }
    };

    return (
      <Form
        defaultValues={{ email: '' }}
        error={error}
        onSubmit={handleSubmit}
      >
        <FormField name="email" label="Email">
          <TextField />
        </FormField>
        <FormButtons>
          <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
        </FormButtons>
      </Form>
    );
  }
  ```

## All form inputs

`FormField` works with all Zen input components. The field automatically binds the `value` and `onChange` props.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormInputsExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Form defaultValues={defaultValues} onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
    <FormField name="name" label="Name">
      <TextField />
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="bio" label="Bio">
      <TextField asTextArea />
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="password" label="Password">
      <PasswordField />
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="search" label="Search">
      <SearchField />
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="country" label="Country">
      <Select items={['USA', 'Canada', 'Mexico']} />
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="newsletter">
      <Checkbox>Subscribe to newsletter</Checkbox>
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="plan" label="Plan">
      <RadioGroup>
        <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
        <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
      </RadioGroup>
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="notifications">
      <Switch>Enable notifications</Switch>
    </FormField>
    <FormField name="volume" label="Volume">
      <Slider />
    </FormField>
    <FormButtons>
      <FormResetButton>Reset</FormResetButton>
      <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
    </FormButtons>
  </Form>
  ```

## Dynamic fields with FormFieldArray

Use `FormFieldArray` when you need to manage a list of fields that can be added or removed dynamically.

  <Box width="300px">
    <FormFieldArrayExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Form
    defaultValues={{ items: [{ name: 'Item 1' }] }}
    onSubmit={handleSubmit}
  >
    <FormFieldArray name="items" label="Items">
      {({ fields, append, remove, control }) => (
        <Column gap>
          {fields.map((field, index) => (
            <Row key={field.id} gap>
              <FormController control={control} name={`items.${index}.name`}>
                {({ field }) => (
                  <TextField
                    value={field.value}
                    onChange={field.onChange}
                  />
                )}
              </FormController>
              <Button onPress={() => remove(index)}>Remove</Button>
            </Row>
          ))}
          <Button onPress={() => append({ name: `Item ${fields.length + 1}` })}>
            Add Item
          </Button>
        </Column>
      )}
    </FormFieldArray>
    <FormButtons>
      <FormResetButton>Reset</FormResetButton>
      <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
    </FormButtons>
  </Form>
  ```

## Accessing form state

The `Form` component accepts a render function as children, giving you access to the full react-hook-form API.

```jsx
<Form defaultValues={{ name: '' }} onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  {({ watch, formState }) => (
    <>
      <FormField name="name" label="Name">
        <TextField />
      </FormField>
      <Text>Current value: {watch('name')}</Text>
      <Text>Form is dirty: {formState.isDirty ? 'Yes' : 'No'}</Text>
      <FormButtons>
        <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
      </FormButtons>
    </>
  )}
</Form>
```

## Schema validation

Use the `resolver` prop to integrate with schema validation libraries like Zod or Yup.

```jsx
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
import { z } from 'zod';

const schema = z.object({
  email: z.string().email('Invalid email'),
  password: z.string().min(8, 'Password must be at least 8 characters'),
});

function MyForm() {
  return (
    <Form
      resolver={zodResolver(schema)}
      onSubmit={handleSubmit}
    >
      <FormField name="email" label="Email">
        <TextField />
      </FormField>
      <FormField name="password" label="Password">
        <PasswordField />
      </FormField>
      <FormButtons>
        <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
      </FormButtons>
    </Form>
  );
}
```

## Controlled forms

Use the `values` prop instead of `defaultValues` when you need to control form values externally. The form will reset when the values change.

```jsx
function EditUserForm({ user }) {
  return (
    <Form
      values={{ name: user.name, email: user.email }}
      onSubmit={handleSubmit}
    >
      <FormField name="name" label="Name">
        <TextField />
      </FormField>
      <FormField name="email" label="Email">
        <TextField />
      </FormField>
      <FormButtons>
        <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Save</FormSubmitButton>
      </FormButtons>
    </Form>
  );
}
```

## Preventing enter key submission

Use `preventSubmit` to stop the form from submitting when the user presses Enter. Useful for forms where you want explicit button clicks only.

```jsx
<Form preventSubmit onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <FormField name="search" label="Search">
    <TextField />
  </FormField>
  <FormButtons>
    <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Search</FormSubmitButton>
  </FormButtons>
</Form>
```

## Component props

### Form

      { name: 'defaultValues', value: 'object', description: 'Initial form values (uncontrolled)' },
      { name: 'values', value: 'object', description: 'Current form values (controlled)' },
      { name: 'onSubmit', value: '(data) => void | Promise', description: 'Called when form is submitted with valid data' },
      { name: 'error', value: 'ReactNode | Error', description: 'Error message to display above the form' },
      { name: 'preventSubmit', value: 'boolean', description: 'Prevents form submission on Enter key' },
      { name: 'resolver', value: 'Resolver', description: 'Validation resolver for schema validation (Zod, Yup, etc.)' },
      { name: 'mode', value: 'string', description: 'Validation mode: "onSubmit" | "onBlur" | "onChange" | "onTouched" | "all"' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### FormField

      { name: 'name', value: 'string', description: 'Field name (required). Must match a key in form values.' },
      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Label displayed above the input' },
      { name: 'description', value: 'string', description: 'Help text displayed below the input' },
      { name: 'rules', value: 'RegisterOptions', description: 'Validation rules (required, min, max, pattern, validate, etc.)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### FormFieldArray

      { name: 'name', value: 'string', description: 'Field array name (required)' },
      { name: 'label', value: 'string', description: 'Label displayed above the field array' },
      { name: 'description', value: 'string', description: 'Help text displayed below the label' },
      { name: 'children', value: '(props) => ReactNode', description: 'Render function receiving fields, append, remove, and control' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### FormSubmitButton

      { name: 'variant', value: 'ButtonVariant', description: 'Button style variant (default: "primary")' },
      { name: 'isDisabled', value: 'boolean', description: 'Override automatic disabled state' },
      { name: 'isLoading', value: 'boolean', description: 'Override automatic loading state' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

### FormResetButton

      { name: 'values', value: 'object', description: 'Values to reset the form to (default: original defaultValues)' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Introduction

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/index.mdx

title: Introduction

# Introduction

**Zen** is a props-driven React component library built for speed. Created by the team at [Umami](https://umami.is),
it lets you build polished interfaces without writing HTML, CSS, or even thinking about Tailwind classes.

The components are built on top of [React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/) for accessibility and
[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling, but you never have to touch either directly.
Just compose components and pass props.

Source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen).

## Why Zen?

Building UI is slow. You have to think about markup structure, CSS organization, responsive breakpoints,
accessibility, and design consistency, all before you can ship a feature.

Zen eliminates that friction. Instead of assembling Tailwind classes or writing custom CSS, you work with
**primitive components** that handle everything through props:

```jsx
<Box padding="12" border borderRadius="lg" shadow="lg">
  <Column alignItems="center" gap="6">
    <Heading size="3xl">Welcome</Heading>
    <Text color="muted" weight="medium">
      This is the Zen way.
    </Text>
    <Button variant="primary">Enter</Button>
  </Column>
</Box>
```
  <Box padding="12" border borderRadius="lg" shadow="lg">
    <Column alignItems="center" gap="6">
      <Heading size="3xl">Welcome</Heading>
      <Text color="muted" weight="medium">{`This is the Zen way.`}</Text>
      <Button variant="primary">Enter</Button>
    </Column>
  </Box>

No `className`. No CSS files. No memorizing utility classes. Just components and props.

## Design out of the box

Zen ships with a complete design system covering
[colors](/docs/design/colors),
[fonts](/docs/design/fonts),
[spacing](/docs/design/spacing),
[shadows](/docs/design/shadows),
and [borders](/docs/design/borders).

Everything works together. The spacing scale is consistent. The colors have proper contrast.
Dark mode just works. You get a professional-looking UI without making design decisions.

Need to customize? Override the CSS variables and the entire system adapts.

## Primitive components

Zen provides building blocks, not pre-built widgets. Components like [Box](/docs/layout/box),
[Row](/docs/layout/row), [Column](/docs/layout/column), and [Grid](/docs/layout/grid)
let you compose any layout through props:

- **Spacing**: `padding`, `margin`, `gap`
- **Layout**: `alignItems`, `justifyContent`, `direction`
- **Responsive**: `{{ base: 'column', md: 'row' }}`
- **Visual**: `border`, `borderRadius`, `shadow`

This is faster than writing Tailwind because you're working at a higher level of abstraction.
You don't assemble classes; you describe what you want.

## Accessibility included

Every interactive component is keyboard-navigable and screen reader-friendly, powered by
[React Aria](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/). Focus management, ARIA attributes,
and interaction patterns are handled automatically.

You don't configure accessibility. You just use the components.

## Props over classes

Zen inverts the typical workflow. Instead of starting with markup and adding styles,
you compose semantic components that already know how to render themselves:

| Traditional approach | Zen approach |
|---------------------|--------------|
| Write HTML structure | Compose components |
| Add Tailwind classes | Pass props |
| Handle responsive manually | Use responsive objects |
| Configure accessibility | Already done |

The result: less code, fewer decisions, faster shipping.

---

# Installation

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/install.mdx

title: Installation

# Installation

Install with your favorite package manager.

```shell
pnpm install @umami/react-zen
```

## Setup

Zen offers two setup options depending on whether your project uses Tailwind CSS.

### Option A: With Tailwind CSS (Recommended)

If your project uses Tailwind CSS v4, use the preset for the best experience with smaller bundle sizes.

#### 1. Configure Tailwind

Add the preset to your `tailwind.config.ts` and include the package in your content paths:

```ts
import zenPreset from '@umami/react-zen/tailwind-preset';

export default {
  presets: [zenPreset],
  content: [
    './src/**/*.{ts,tsx}',
    './node_modules/@umami/react-zen/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}',
  ],
};
```

#### 2. Import styles

Import the minimal stylesheet which includes theme CSS variables and component animations:

```js
import '@umami/react-zen/styles.css';
```

### Option B: Without Tailwind CSS

If your project doesn't use Tailwind, import the full stylesheet which includes all necessary utility classes:

```js
import '@umami/react-zen/styles.full.css';
```

This is a self-contained CSS file with no additional configuration needed.

## Add ZenProvider

Wrap your application with `ZenProvider` to enable theming and toast notifications.

```jsx
import { ZenProvider } from '@umami/react-zen';

export default function App({ children }) {
  return (
    <ZenProvider>
      {children}
    </ZenProvider>
  );
}
```

`ZenProvider` accepts the following props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `colorScheme` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | `'system'` | Initial color scheme |
| `toast` | `ToasterProps` | `{ duration: 3000 }` | Toast notification settings |

## Use components

```jsx
import { Button } from '@umami/react-zen';

export function Component() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Button</Button>;
}
```
  <Button variant="primary">Button</Button>

# Box

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/layout/box.mdx

title: Box

# Box

A versatile layout primitive that serves as the foundation for building UI. Box provides comprehensive styling props for spacing, colors, borders, positioning, and more. Use it to wrap and position other components, create cards, or build custom layouts.

  <Box>I am a box.</Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box>I am a box.</Box>
  ```

## With properties

  <Box padding="5" shadow="lg" borderRadius="lg" border>
    I am a box.
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box padding="5" shadow="lg" borderRadius="lg" border>
    I am a box.
  </Box>
  ```

## Responsive sizing

Use Tailwind preset values for width and height with responsive breakpoints. Resize your browser window to see this box change width: full width on mobile, half width on medium screens, and one-third on large screens.

<Example alignItems="stretch">
  <Box width={{ base: 'full', md: '1/2', lg: '1/3' }} padding="4" backgroundColor="surface-raised" border borderRadius>
    Responsive width
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box
    width={{ base: 'full', md: '1/2', lg: '1/3' }}
    padding="4"
    backgroundColor="surface-raised"
    border
    borderRadius>
    Responsive width
  </Box>
  ```

## State styles

Apply styles for hover, focus, and active states using object props. Each state accepts `color`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, and `opacity`.

  <Box
    padding="4"
    border
    borderRadius
    cursor="pointer"
    hover={{ color: 'red-600', backgroundColor: "red-100", borderColor: "red-500" }}
    Hover over me
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box
    padding="4"
    border
    borderRadius
    cursor="pointer"
    hover={{
      color: 'red-600',
      backgroundColor: "red-100",
      borderColor: "red-500"
    }}>
    Hover over me
  </Box>
  ```

### Multiple states

Click to focus, then hover and click to see all states.

  <Box
    tabIndex={0}
    padding="4"
    backgroundColor="surface-base"
    border
    borderRadius
    cursor="pointer"
    hover={{ backgroundColor: "blue-50" }}
    focus={{ borderColor: "blue-500" }}
    active={{ backgroundColor: "blue-100", opacity: "50" }}
    Interactive box (hover, focus, active)
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <Box
    tabIndex={0}
    padding="4"
    backgroundColor="surface-base"
    border
    borderRadius
    cursor="pointer"
    hover={{ backgroundColor: "blue-50" }}
    focus={{ borderColor: "blue-500" }}
    active={{ backgroundColor: "blue-100", opacity: "50" }}
  >
    Interactive box (hover, focus, active)
  </Box>
  ```

      { name: 'bottom', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'left', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'overflow', value: 'Responsive<Overflow>', description: '"visible" | "hidden" | "clip" | "scroll" | "auto"' },
      { name: 'overflowX', value: 'Responsive<Overflow>', description: '"visible" | "hidden" | "clip" | "scroll" | "auto"' },
      { name: 'overflowY', value: 'Responsive<Overflow>', description: '"visible" | "hidden" | "clip" | "scroll" | "auto"' },

      { name: 'justifySelf', value: 'Responsive<JustifySelf>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | ...' },
      { name: 'flexBasis', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'flexGrow', value: 'string | number', description: 'Inline style' },
      { name: 'flexShrink', value: 'string | number', description: 'Inline style' },
      { name: 'gridArea', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'gridRow', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'gridColumn', value: 'string', description: 'CSS value (inline style)' },
      { name: 'order', value: 'number', description: 'Inline style' },
      { name: 'zIndex', value: 'number', description: 'Inline style' },
      { name: 'hover', value: 'StateStyles', description: '{ color?, backgroundColor?, borderColor?, opacity? }' },
      { name: 'focus', value: 'StateStyles', description: '{ color?, backgroundColor?, borderColor?, opacity? }' },
      { name: 'active', value: 'StateStyles', description: '{ color?, backgroundColor?, borderColor?, opacity? }' },
      { name: 'as', value: 'string', description: 'HTML element to render' },
      { name: 'render', value: 'RenderProp', description: 'Render prop for polymorphism' },

    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

---

# Container

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/layout/container.mdx

title: Container

# Container

A centered wrapper that constrains content to a maximum width. Essential for readable line lengths and consistent page layouts, especially for text-heavy content like articles or documentation.

  <DialogTrigger>
    <Button>Show container</Button>
    <Modal>
      <Dialog>
        <Container>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt
          ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation
          ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in
          reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur
          sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id
          est laborum.
        </Container>
      </Dialog>
    </Modal>
  </DialogTrigger>

  ```jsx
  <Container>
    <Text>Content constrained to max-width</Text>
  </Container>
  ```

The container at each breakpoint has a `max-width`.

      { name: 'xs', width: '520px', maxWidth: '500px' },
      { name: 'sm', width: '768px', maxWidth: '740px' },
      { name: 'md', width: '1024px', maxWidth: '1000px' },
      { name: 'lg', width: '1280px', maxWidth: '1240px' },
      { name: 'xl', width: '1640px', maxWidth: '1600px' },
    <DataColumn id="name" label="Size" />
    <DataColumn id="width" label="Breakpoint" />
    <DataColumn id="maxWidth" label="Max width" />

## Component props

      { name: 'isCentered', value: 'boolean', description: 'Centers the container horizontally (default: true)' },
      { name: 'isFluid', value: 'boolean', description: 'Makes the container full width with no max-width constraint' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

Container also extends all [Box](/docs/layout/box) props.

---

# Flexbox

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/layout/flexbox.mdx

title: Flexbox

# Flexbox

A flexible layout component using CSS Flexbox for one-dimensional arrangements. Provides fine-grained control over alignment, distribution, and wrapping. For common cases, prefer the simpler Row and Column components.

<Example gap="8">
  <Column alignItems="center">
    <Label>Row</Label>
    <Flexbox direction="row" gap="3">
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
    </Flexbox>
  </Column>
  <Column>
    <Label>Column</Label>
    <Flexbox direction="column" gap="3">
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
    </Flexbox>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Column alignItems="center">
    <Label>Row</Label>
    <Flexbox direction="row" gap="3">
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
    </Flexbox>
  </Column>
  <Column>
    <Label>Column</Label>
    <Flexbox direction="column" gap="3">
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
      <ExampleBox />
    </Flexbox>
  </Column>
  ```

There are convenience components `Row` and `Column` which render a `Flexbox` with the direction pre-selected. You should opt to use them
by default as they provide more semantic meaning and are easier to read.

## Component props

A Flexbox renders a [Box](/docs/layout/box) as a child, so it also accepts all Box props.

      { name: 'display', value: 'Responsive<FlexDisplay>', description: '"flex" | "inline-flex" | "none"' },
      { name: 'direction', value: 'Responsive<FlexDirection>', description: '"row" | "column" | "row-reverse" | "column-reverse"' },
      { name: 'wrap', value: 'Responsive<FlexWrap>', description: '"wrap" | "nowrap" | "wrap-reverse"' },
      { name: 'justifyContent', value: 'Responsive<JustifyContent>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "space-between" | "space-around" | ...' },
      { name: 'justifyItems', value: 'Responsive<JustifyItems>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline" | ...' },
      { name: 'alignContent', value: 'Responsive<AlignContent>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "space-between" | "stretch" | ...' },
      { name: 'alignItems', value: 'Responsive<AlignItems>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline" | ...' },
      { name: 'gap', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
      { name: 'gapX', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
      { name: 'gapY', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
      { name: 'as', value: 'string', description: 'HTML element to render' },
      { name: 'render', value: 'RenderProp', description: 'Render prop for polymorphism' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

---

# Grid

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/layout/grid.mdx

title: Grid

# Grid

A CSS Grid layout component for creating two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns. Ideal for building responsive page layouts, card grids, dashboards, and any design requiring precise control over both horizontal and vertical alignment.

  <Grid gap="3" columns="3">
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>

  ```jsx
  <Grid gap="3" columns="3">
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>
  ```

## Responsive columns

Use responsive objects to change the grid layout at different breakpoints.

  <Grid gap="3" columns={{ base: '1', sm: '2', lg: '4' }}>
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>

  ```jsx
  <Grid gap="3" columns={{ base: '1', sm: '2', lg: '4' }}>
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>
  ```

## Custom templates

For complex layouts, pass a custom CSS grid-template string.

  <Grid gap="3" columns="200px 1fr 1fr">
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>

  ```jsx
  <Grid gap="3" columns="200px 1fr 1fr">
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>
  ```

## Responsive custom templates

Custom CSS templates can also be responsive by passing an object with breakpoint keys.

  <Grid gap="3" columns={{ base: '1fr', lg: 'auto 1fr' }}>
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>

  ```jsx
  <Grid gap="3" columns={{ base: '1fr', lg: 'auto 1fr' }}>
    <ExampleBox />
    <ExampleBox />
  </Grid>
  ```

## Grid item placement

  <Grid gap="3" columns="3" rows="3">
    <ExampleBox width="auto" gridRow="1 / 2" gridColumn="1 / 3" />
    <ExampleBox width="auto" height="auto" gridRow="2 / 4" gridColumn="1 / 3" />
    <ExampleBox height="auto" gridRow="1 / 4" gridColumn="3 / 4" />
  </Grid>

  ```jsx
  <Grid gap="3" columns="3" rows="3">
    <ExampleBox width="auto" gridRow="1 / 2" gridColumn="1 / 3" />
    <ExampleBox width="auto" height="auto" gridRow="2 / 4" gridColumn="1 / 3" />
    <ExampleBox height="auto" gridRow="1 / 4" gridColumn="3 / 4" />
  </Grid>
  ```

## Component props

Grid extends [Box](/docs/layout/box) and accepts all Box props.

      { name: 'display', value: 'Responsive<GridDisplay>', description: '"grid" | "inline-grid" | "none"' },
      { name: 'columns', value: 'Responsive<GridColumns | string>', description: '"1"-"12" | "none" | "subgrid" | custom CSS template' },
      { name: 'rows', value: 'Responsive<GridRows | string>', description: '"1"-"12" | "none" | "subgrid" | custom CSS template' },
      { name: 'autoFlow', value: 'Responsive<GridAutoFlow>', description: '"row" | "column" | "dense" | "row-dense" | "column-dense"' },
      { name: 'justifyContent', value: 'Responsive<JustifyContent>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "space-between" | "space-around" | ...' },
      { name: 'justifyItems', value: 'Responsive<JustifyItems>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline" | ...' },
      { name: 'alignContent', value: 'Responsive<AlignContent>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "space-between" | "stretch" | ...' },
      { name: 'alignItems', value: 'Responsive<AlignItems>', description: '"center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline" | ...' },
      { name: 'gap', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
      { name: 'gapX', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
      { name: 'gapY', value: 'Responsive<Gap>', description: 'true | Spacing scale' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

# Blockquote

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/typography/blockquote.mdx

title: Blockquote

# Blockquote

The blockquote element represents a section that is quoted from another source.

  <Blockquote>
    {`I have a dream that one day this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed:
    'We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.' I have a dream that
    one day on the red hills of Georgia, the sons of former slaves and the sons of former slave
    owners will be able to sit down together at the table of brotherhood.`}
  </Blockquote>

  ```jsx
  <Blockquote>
    {`I have a dream that one day this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed:
    'We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.' I have a dream that
    one day on the red hills of Georgia, the sons of former slaves and the sons of former slave
    owners will be able to sit down together at the table of brotherhood.`}
  </Blockquote>
  ```

## Component props

      { name: 'children', value: 'ReactNode', description: 'Quote content' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Description" />

# Heading

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/typography/heading.mdx

title: Heading

# Heading

A semantic heading component for titles and section headers. Supports multiple sizes and semantic HTML levels (h1-h6) for proper document structure and accessibility.

  <Heading>Hello.</Heading>

  ```jsx
  <Heading>Hello.</Heading>
  ```

## Sizes

  <Heading size="sm">Heading sm</Heading>
  <Heading size="base">Heading base</Heading>
  <Heading size="lg">Heading lg</Heading>
  <Heading size="xl">Heading xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="2xl">Heading 2xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="3xl">Heading 3xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="4xl">Heading 4xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="5xl">Heading 5xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="6xl">Heading 6xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="7xl">Heading 7xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="8xl">Heading 8xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="9xl">Heading 9xl</Heading>

  ```jsx
  <Heading size="sm">Heading sm</Heading>
  <Heading size="base">Heading base</Heading>
  <Heading size="lg">Heading lg</Heading>
  <Heading size="xl">Heading xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="2xl">Heading 2xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="3xl">Heading 3xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="4xl">Heading 4xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="5xl">Heading 5xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="6xl">Heading 6xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="7xl">Heading 7xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="8xl">Heading 8xl</Heading>
  <Heading size="9xl">Heading 9xl</Heading>
  ```

## Component props

Heading extends [Text](/docs/typography/text) and accepts all Text props. Default values are `size="2xl"`, `weight="semibold"`, and `spacing="tight"`.

      { name: 'size', value: 'Responsive<HeadingSize>', description: '"sm" | "base" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | ... | "9xl"' },
      { name: 'as', value: 'HeadingElement', description: '"h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" (default: "h2")' },
    <DataColumn id="description" label="Values" />

## Letter spacing

  <Column gap="2">
    <Row gap="4" alignItems="center"><Label className="w-16">tighter</Label><Text spacing="tighter">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text></Row>
    <Row gap="4" alignItems="center"><Label className="w-16">tight</Label><Text spacing="tight">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text></Row>
    <Row gap="4" alignItems="center"><Label className="w-16">normal</Label><Text spacing="normal">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text></Row>
    <Row gap="4" alignItems="center"><Label className="w-16">wide</Label><Text spacing="wide">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text></Row>
    <Row gap="4" alignItems="center"><Label className="w-16">wider</Label><Text spacing="wider">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text></Row>
  </Column>

  ```jsx

  <Text spacing="wide">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text>
  <Text spacing="wider">The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text>
  ```

    </Column>

      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Column>


## Whitespace

Control how whitespace is handled within text.

  <Column gap="4">
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>normal</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '300px' }}>
        <Text whitespace="normal" as="div">Multiple   spaces   collapse    and text wraps normally.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>nowrap</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '300px' }}>
        <Text whitespace="nowrap" as="div">This text will not wrap to the next line.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>pre</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '300px' }}>
        <Text whitespace="pre" as="div">{'Preserves   spaces\nand newlines.'}</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>pre-wrap</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '300px' }}>
        <Text whitespace="pre-wrap" as="div">{'Preserves   spaces\nand wraps text.'}</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Text whitespace="normal" as="div">Multiple   spaces   collapse    and text wraps normally.</Text>
  <Text whitespace="nowrap" as="div">This text will not wrap to the next line.</Text>
  <Text whitespace="pre" as="div">{'Preserves   spaces\nand newlines.'}</Text>
  <Text whitespace="pre-wrap" as="div">{'Preserves   spaces\nand wraps text.'}</Text>
  ```

## Word break

Control how words break when reaching the end of a line.

  <Column gap="4">
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>normal</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '150px' }}>
        <Text wordBreak="normal" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>words</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '150px' }}>
        <Text wordBreak="words" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>all</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md" style={{ width: '150px' }}>
        <Text wordBreak="all" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Text wordBreak="normal" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
  <Text wordBreak="words" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
  <Text wordBreak="all" as="div">Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious</Text>
  ```

## Vertical align

Control vertical alignment of inline elements. Useful for superscript, subscript, and aligning text with icons.

  <Column gap="4">
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>Superscript</Label>
      <Text size="lg">E = mc<Text verticalAlign="super" size="xs">2</Text></Text>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>Subscript</Label>
      <Text size="lg">H<Text verticalAlign="sub" size="xs">2</Text>O</Text>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>Top</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text>
          <Box as="span" className="inline-block w-6 h-6 bg-blue-500 rounded mr-2" />
          <Text verticalAlign="top">aligned to top</Text>
        </Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>Middle</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text>
          <Box as="span" className="inline-block w-6 h-6 bg-green-500 rounded mr-2" />
          <Text verticalAlign="middle">aligned to middle</Text>
        </Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>Bottom</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text>
          <Box as="span" className="inline-block w-6 h-6 bg-orange-500 rounded mr-2" />
          <Text verticalAlign="bottom">aligned to bottom</Text>
        </Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Text size="lg">E = mc<Text verticalAlign="super" size="xs">2</Text></Text>
  <Text size="lg">H<Text verticalAlign="sub" size="xs">2</Text>O</Text>
  <Text verticalAlign="top">aligned to top</Text>
  <Text verticalAlign="middle">aligned to middle</Text>
  <Text verticalAlign="bottom">aligned to bottom</Text>
  ```

## Text indent

Indent the first line of text.

  <Column gap="4">
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>indent 4</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text indent="4" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>indent 8</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text indent="8" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="1">
      <Label>indent 12</Label>
      <Box border padding="2" borderRadius="md">
        <Text indent="12" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Text indent="4" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</Text>
  <Text indent="8" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</Text>
  <Text indent="12" as="div">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</Text>
  ```

# Usage Guide

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/docs/usage.mdx

title: Usage Guide

# Usage Guide

This guide covers the core patterns and best practices for building UIs with Zen.
Understanding these concepts will help you write cleaner, more maintainable code.

## Component Categories

Zen components fall into two categories, each with a distinct purpose:

### Layout Components

Layout components handle **positioning, spacing, and structure**. They accept a full set of styling props.

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| [Box](/docs/layout/box) | General-purpose container with all styling props |
| [Row](/docs/layout/row) | Horizontal flex layout |
| [Column](/docs/layout/column) | Vertical flex layout |
| [Grid](/docs/layout/grid) | CSS grid layout |
| [Container](/docs/layout/container) | Centered, max-width container |

```jsx
<Column gap="4" padding="6">
  <Row justifyContent="space-between" alignItems="center">
    <Heading>Title</Heading>
    <Button>Action</Button>
  </Row>
  <Text>Content goes here</Text>
</Column>
```

### Interactive Components

Interactive components handle **user interaction and display**. They focus on their core functionality
and delegate layout concerns to their parent.

Examples: `Button`, `TextField`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `Tabs`, etc.

## The Composition Pattern

A key principle in Zen is **separation of concerns**: interactive components handle behavior,
layout components handle positioning.

### Positioning with Box

When you need to position or add spacing to an interactive component, wrap it in a layout component:

```jsx
// Align a button to the end of its container
<Box alignSelf="end">
  <Button>Submit</Button>
</Box>

// Add margin to a text field
<Box marginBottom="4">
  <TextField label="Email" />
</Box>

// Position a checkbox absolutely
<Box position="absolute" top="4" right="4">
  <Checkbox>Select</Checkbox>
</Box>
```

  <Row justifyContent="space-between" alignItems="start" gap="4" padding="4" border borderRadius="lg">
    <Column gap="2">
      <Text weight="medium">Form Section</Text>
      <Text size="sm" color="muted">Fill out the details below</Text>
    </Column>
    <Box alignSelf="end">
      <Button variant="primary" size="sm">Save</Button>
    </Box>
  </Row>

### Why This Pattern?

1. **Focused APIs** - Button handles button concerns, Box handles layout concerns
2. **Flexibility** - Any component can be positioned any way without special props
3. **Predictability** - Layout is always handled by layout components
4. **Smaller bundle** - Interactive components don't carry unused layout prop logic

## Building Layouts

### Use Semantic Layout Components

Prefer `Row` and `Column` over `Box` with flex direction:

```jsx
// Preferred
<Row gap="4" alignItems="center">
  <Avatar />
  <Text>Username</Text>
</Row>

// Avoid
<Box display="flex" direction="row" gap="4" alignItems="center">
  <Avatar />
  <Text>Username</Text>
</Box>
```

### Spacing with Gap

Use `gap` for consistent spacing between children instead of individual margins:

```jsx
// Preferred - consistent spacing
<Column gap="4">
  <TextField label="Name" />
  <TextField label="Email" />
  <TextField label="Message" />
</Column>

// Avoid - manual margins
<Column>
  <Box marginBottom="4"><TextField label="Name" /></Box>
  <Box marginBottom="4"><TextField label="Email" /></Box>
  <TextField label="Message" />
</Column>
```

### Container for Page Content

Use `Container` to center and constrain page content:

```jsx
<Container maxWidth="lg" padding="6">
  <Column gap="8">
    <Heading>Page Title</Heading>
    <Text>Page content...</Text>
  </Column>
</Container>
```

## Responsive Design

### Responsive Props

Most style props accept responsive objects. Use `base` for mobile-first styles:

```jsx
<Heading size={{ base: 'xl', md: '3xl', lg: '5xl' }}>
  Responsive Heading
</Heading>

<Grid columns={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap="4">
  <Card>Item 1</Card>
  <Card>Item 2</Card>
  <Card>Item 3</Card>
</Grid>

<Row
  direction={{ base: 'column', md: 'row' }}
  gap={{ base: '4', md: '8' }}
>
  <Box>Sidebar</Box>
  <Box>Main content</Box>
</Row>
```

  <Grid columns={{ base: 1, sm: 2 }} gap="4">
    <Box padding="4" backgroundColor="surface-raised" borderRadius="md">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted">Resize to see layout change</Text>
    </Box>
    <Box padding="4" backgroundColor="surface-raised" borderRadius="md">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted">Stacks on mobile</Text>
    </Box>
  </Grid>

### Breakpoints

| Name | Min Width | Typical Device |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| `base` | 0px | All devices (mobile-first) |
| `sm` | 640px | Large phones, small tablets |
| `md` | 768px | Tablets |
| `lg` | 1024px | Laptops |
| `xl` | 1280px | Desktops |
| `2xl` | 1536px | Large desktops |

## Styling Props

### Common Props by Category

**Spacing:**
```jsx
<Box padding="4" paddingX="6" margin="2" marginTop="8" />
```

**Layout:**
```jsx
<Row alignItems="center" justifyContent="space-between" gap="4" />
```

**Visual:**
```jsx
<Box border borderRadius="lg" shadow="md" backgroundColor="surface-raised" />
```

**Position:**
```jsx
<Box position="absolute" top="0" right="0" />
```

### Using className

For styles not covered by props, use `className` with Tailwind utilities:

```jsx
<Box
  padding="4"
  border
  className="hover:shadow-lg transition-shadow"
>
  Hover me
</Box>
```

## Forms

### Basic Form Layout

Use `Column` with consistent `gap` for form fields:

```jsx
<Column gap="4">
  <TextField label="Name" placeholder="Enter your name" />
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
  <TextArea label="Message" placeholder="Your message..." />
  <Row justifyContent="end" gap="2">
    <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
    <Button variant="primary">Submit</Button>
  </Row>
</Column>
```

  <Box padding="6" border borderRadius="lg" maxWidth="400px">
    <Column gap="4">
      <TextField label="Name" placeholder="Enter your name" />
      <TextField label="Email" type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
      <Row justifyContent="end" gap="2">
        <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
        <Button variant="primary">Submit</Button>
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Box>

### Form with react-hook-form

Zen provides form integration components:

```jsx
import { Form, FormField, FormSubmitButton } from '@umami/react-zen';
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';

function MyForm() {
  const form = useForm({ defaultValues: { email: '' } });

  return (
    <Form form={form} onSubmit={data => console.log(data)}>
      <Column gap="4">
        <FormField name="email" label="Email" rules={{ required: 'Required' }}>
          <TextField placeholder="you@example.com" />
        </FormField>
        <FormSubmitButton variant="primary">Submit</FormSubmitButton>
      </Column>
    </Form>
  );
}
```

## Theming

### Light and Dark Mode

Zen supports light and dark modes out of the box. Use `ZenProvider` to initialize:

```jsx
<ZenProvider colorScheme="system">
  <App />
</ZenProvider>
```

Toggle programmatically with the `useTheme` hook:

```jsx
import { useTheme } from '@umami/react-zen';

function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();

  return (
    <Button onPress={() => setTheme(theme === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light')}>
      Toggle Theme
    </Button>
  );
}
```

### Semantic Colors

Use semantic color tokens that adapt to the theme:

```jsx
// These automatically adjust for light/dark mode
<Box backgroundColor="surface-raised" />
<Text color="muted" />
<Box borderColor="edge-muted" />
```

| Token | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `surface-base` | Page background |
| `surface-raised` | Cards, elevated elements |
| `surface-sunken` | Inset areas |
| `primary` | Primary text |
| `muted` | Secondary text |
| `disabled` | Disabled state |

## Component Patterns

### Cards

```jsx
<Box padding="6" border borderRadius="lg" shadow="sm" backgroundColor="surface-base">
  <Column gap="4">
    <Heading size="lg">Card Title</Heading>
    <Text color="muted">Card description or content goes here.</Text>
    <Row gap="2">
      <Button variant="primary" size="sm">Action</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</Box>
```

  <Box padding="6" border borderRadius="lg" shadow="sm" backgroundColor="surface-base" maxWidth="300px">
    <Column gap="4">
      <Heading size="lg">Card Title</Heading>
      <Text color="muted">Card description or content goes here.</Text>
      <Row gap="2">
        <Button variant="primary" size="sm">Action</Button>
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Box>

### Page Header

```jsx
<Row justifyContent="space-between" alignItems="center" marginBottom="8">
  <Column gap="1">
    <Heading size="2xl">Dashboard</Heading>
    <Text color="muted">Welcome back, here's what's happening.</Text>
  </Column>
  <Row gap="2">
    <Button variant="outline">Export</Button>
    <Button variant="primary">Create New</Button>
  </Row>
</Row>
```

  <Row justifyContent="space-between" alignItems="center" gap="4" padding="4" border borderRadius="lg">
    <Column gap="1">
      <Heading size="2xl">Dashboard</Heading>
      <Text color="muted">Welcome back, here's what's happening.</Text>
    </Column>
    <Row gap="2">
      <Button variant="outline">Export</Button>
      <Button variant="primary">Create New</Button>
    </Row>
  </Row>

### Empty State

```jsx
<Column alignItems="center" gap="4" padding="12">
  <Box className="text-foreground-muted">
    <Lucide.Inbox size={48} />
  </Box>
  <Column alignItems="center" gap="2">
    <Heading size="lg">No items yet</Heading>
    <Text color="muted" align="center">
      Get started by creating your first item.
    </Text>
  </Column>
  <Button variant="primary">Create Item</Button>
</Column>
```

  <Column alignItems="center" gap="4" padding="12" border borderRadius="lg">
    <Box className="text-foreground-muted">
      <Lucide.Inbox size={48} />
    </Box>
    <Column alignItems="center" gap="2">
      <Heading size="lg">No items yet</Heading>
      <Text color="muted" align="center">
        Get started by creating your first item.
      </Text>
    </Column>
    <Button variant="primary">Create Item</Button>
  </Column>

## Tips

1. **Start with layout** - Build the structure with Row/Column/Grid first, then add content
2. **Use gap over margin** - Cleaner and more maintainable for spacing between siblings
3. **Wrap for positioning** - Use Box to position interactive components
4. **Think responsive** - Use responsive objects for props that should adapt
5. **Leverage semantics** - Use semantic colors and tokens for theme compatibility
6. **Keep it simple** - Compose simple components rather than configuring complex ones

    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Tabs */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Tabs</Text>
      <Tabs>
        <TabList>
          <Tab id="overview">Overview</Tab>
          <Tab id="analytics">Analytics</Tab>
          <Tab id="settings">Settings</Tab>
        </TabList>
        <TabPanel id="overview"><Text color="muted" size="sm">Overview content</Text></TabPanel>
        <TabPanel id="analytics"><Text color="muted" size="sm">Analytics content</Text></TabPanel>
        <TabPanel id="settings"><Text color="muted" size="sm">Settings content</Text></TabPanel>
      </Tabs>
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Accordion */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Accordion</Text>
      <Accordion type="single">
        <AccordionItem id="1">
          <>What is Zen?</>
          <Text size="sm" color="muted">A props-driven React component library.</Text>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem id="2">
          <>Is it accessible?</>
          <Text size="sm" color="muted">Yes, built on React Aria.</Text>
        </AccordionItem>
        <AccordionItem id="3">
          <>Can I customize it?</>
          <Text size="sm" color="muted">Yes, with CSS variables.</Text>
        </AccordionItem>
      </Accordion>
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Breadcrumbs */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Breadcrumbs</Text>
      <Breadcrumbs>
        <Breadcrumb>Home</Breadcrumb>
        <Breadcrumb>Products</Breadcrumb>
        <Breadcrumb>Category</Breadcrumb>
        <Breadcrumb>Item</Breadcrumb>
      </Breadcrumbs>
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Toggle Group */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Toggle Group</Text>

        <ToggleGroupItem id="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem id="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem id="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Loading */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Loading</Text>
      <Row gap="4" alignItems="center">
        <Spinner size="sm" />
        <Spinner size="md" />
        <Spinner size="lg" />
        <Dots />
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Calendar */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>
    <Column gap="3">
      <Text size="sm" color="muted" weight="medium">Calendar</Text>
      <Calendar />
    </Column>
  </Box>

  {/* Code */}
  <Box padding="5" border borderRadius="lg" marginBottom="6" backgroundColor="surface-base" style={{ breakInside: 'avoid' }}>

    </Column>

# Empty State

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/patterns/data-display/empty-state.mdx

title: Empty State

# Empty State

A placeholder display for when there's no content to show, with icon, message, and optional call-to-action. Built using `Box`, `Column`, `Icon`, `Text`, and `Button` components.

  <EmptyState
    icon={<Lucide.Inbox />}
    title="No messages"
    description="You don't have any messages yet. Start a conversation to see them here."
  />

```jsx
import { Inbox } from 'lucide-react';
import { EmptyState } from './EmptyState';

<EmptyState
  icon={<Inbox />}
  title="No messages"
  description="You don't have any messages yet. Start a conversation to see them here."
  action={{ label: "Compose Message", onClick: () => console.log('Compose') }}
/>
```

## Source

<ExampleCode>
```jsx
'use client';

import { FileX, Inbox, Search } from 'lucide-react';
import { Box, Button, Column, Icon, Row, Text } from '@umami/react-zen';

export function EmptyState({
  icon,
  title,
  description,
  action,
  secondaryAction,
  ...props
}) {
  return (
    <Column alignItems="center" justifyContent="center" padding="8" gap="4" {...props}>
      {icon && (
        <Row
          width="16"
          height="16"
          borderRadius="full"
          backgroundColor="surface-raised"
          alignItems="center"
          justifyContent="center"
        >
          <Icon size="lg" color="muted">{icon}</Icon>
        </Row>
      )}
      <Column alignItems="center" gap="2">
        <Text size="lg" weight="semibold">{title}</Text>
        {description && (
          <Box maxWidth="20rem" textAlign="center">
            <Text color="muted">{description}</Text>
          </Box>
        )}
      </Column>
      {(action || secondaryAction) && (
        <Column gap="2" alignItems="center">
          {action && <Button variant="primary" onPress={action.onClick}>{action.label}</Button>}
          {secondaryAction && <Button variant="quiet" onPress={secondaryAction.onClick}>{secondaryAction.label}</Button>}
        </Column>
      )}
    </Column>
  );
}

export function EmptyStateNoResults(props) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<Search />}
      title="No results found"
      description="Try adjusting your search or filter to find what you're looking for."
      {...props}
    />
  );
}

export function EmptyStateNoData(props) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<Inbox />}
      title="No data yet"
      description="Get started by creating your first item."
      {...props}
    />
  );
}

export function EmptyStateError(props) {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      icon={<FileX />}
      title="Something went wrong"
      description="We couldn't load this content. Please try again."
      action={{ label: 'Try again', onClick: () => window.location.reload() }}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
```
</ExampleCode>

## Variations

### No search results

  <EmptyStateNoResults />

```jsx
<EmptyStateNoResults />
```

### No data

  <EmptyStateNoData />

```jsx
<EmptyStateNoData
  action={{ label: "Create First Item", onClick: () => {} }}
/>
```

### Error state

  <Column alignItems="center" justifyContent="center" padding="8" gap="4">
    <Row width="16" height="16" borderRadius="full" backgroundColor="surface-raised" alignItems="center" justifyContent="center">
      <Icon size="lg" color="muted"><Lucide.FileX /></Icon>
    </Row>
    <Column alignItems="center" gap="2">
      <Text size="lg" weight="semibold">Something went wrong</Text>
      <Box maxWidth="20rem" textAlign="center"><Text color="muted">We couldn't load this content. Please try again.</Text></Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2" alignItems="center">
      <Button variant="primary">Try Again</Button>
      <Button variant="quiet">Contact Support</Button>
    </Column>
  </Column>

```jsx
<EmptyStateError
  action={{ label: "Try Again", onClick: () => window.location.reload() }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: "Contact Support", onClick: () => {} }}
/>
```

### Custom empty state

  <Column alignItems="center" justifyContent="center" padding="8" gap="4">
    <Row width="16" height="16" borderRadius="full" backgroundColor="surface-raised" alignItems="center" justifyContent="center">
      <Icon size="lg" color="muted"><Lucide.FolderOpen /></Icon>
    </Row>
    <Column alignItems="center" gap="2">
      <Text size="lg" weight="semibold">No projects</Text>
      <Box maxWidth="20rem" textAlign="center"><Text color="muted">Create a new project to get started building something amazing.</Text></Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2" alignItems="center">
      <Button variant="primary">New Project</Button>
      <Button variant="quiet">Import Existing</Button>
    </Column>
  </Column>

```jsx
<EmptyState
  icon={<FolderOpen />}
  title="No projects"
  description="Create a new project to get started building something amazing."
  action={{ label: "New Project", onClick: () => {} }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: "Import Existing", onClick: () => {} }}
/>
```

### Minimal (no icon)

  <EmptyState
    title="Nothing here yet"
    description="This section is empty."
  />

```jsx

  title="Nothing here yet"
  description="This section is empty."
/>
```

# Icon Label

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/patterns/data-display/icon-label.mdx

title: Icon Label

# Icon Label

A simple pattern for pairing an icon with text. This is one of the most common UI patterns and is easily composed using the `Row`, `Icon`, and `Text` components.

  <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Settings />} label="Settings" />

```jsx
<IconLabel icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" />
```

## Source

<ExampleCode>
```jsx
'use client';

import { Icon, Row, Text } from '@umami/react-zen';

export function IconLabel({ icon, label, size = 'md', children, ...props }) {
  const iconSize = size === 'sm' ? 'sm' : size === 'lg' ? 'lg' : 'md';
  const textSize = size === 'sm' ? 'sm' : size === 'lg' ? 'lg' : 'base';

  return (
    <Row alignItems="center" gap="2" {...props}>
      <Icon size={iconSize}>{icon}</Icon>
      {label && <Text size={textSize}>{label}</Text>}
      {children}
    </Row>
  );
}
```
</ExampleCode>

## Variations

### Different sizes

<Example direction="column" gap="4">
  <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Star />} label="Small" size="sm" />
  <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Star />} label="Medium" size="md" />
  <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Star />} label="Large" size="lg" />

```jsx
<IconLabel icon={<Star />} label="Small" size="sm" />
<IconLabel icon={<Star />} label="Medium" size="md" />
<IconLabel icon={<Star />} label="Large" size="lg" />
```

### As a button

  <Button variant="outline">
    <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Download />} label="Download" size="sm" />
  </Button>

```jsx
<Button variant="outline">
  <IconLabel icon={<Download />} label="Download" size="sm" />
</Button>
```

### With children instead of label

  <IconLabel icon={<Lucide.Mail />}>
    <Text>Messages</Text>
    <Text color="muted">(3 unread)</Text>
  </IconLabel>

```jsx
<IconLabel icon={<Mail />}>
  <Text>Messages</Text>
  <Text color="muted">(3 unread)</Text>
</IconLabel>
```

# List Row

Source: https://github.com/umami-software/react-zen/blob/master/apps/docs/content/patterns/data-display/list-item.mdx

title: List Row

# List Row

A configurable list row with avatar, title, description, meta, and actions. Built using `Box`, `Row`, `Column`, `Icon`, and `Text` components.

  <Box border borderRadius="lg" overflow="hidden">
    <ListRow>
      <ListRowAvatar fallback="JD" />
      <ListRowContent title="John Doe" description="john@example.com" meta="Admin" />
    </ListRow>
    <ListRow>
      <ListRowAvatar fallback="JS" />
      <ListRowContent title="Jane Smith" description="jane@example.com" meta="User" />
    </ListRow>
    <ListRow>
      <ListRowAvatar fallback="BW" />
      <ListRowContent title="Bob Wilson" description="bob@example.com" meta="User" />
    </ListRow>
  </Box>

```jsx
<Box border borderRadius="lg" overflow="hidden">
  <ListRow>
    <ListRowAvatar fallback="JD" />
    <ListRowContent title="John Doe" description="john@example.com" meta="Admin" />
  </ListRow>
  <ListRow>
    <ListRowAvatar fallback="JS" />
    <ListRowContent title="Jane Smith" description="jane@example.com" meta="User" />
  </ListRow>
  <ListRow>
    <ListRowAvatar fallback="BW" />
    <ListRowContent title="Bob Wilson" description="bob@example.com" meta="User" />
  </ListRow>
</Box>
```

## Source

<ExampleCode>
```jsx
'use client';

import { ChevronRight } from 'lucide-react';
import { Box, Column, Icon, Row, Text } from '@umami/react-zen';

export function ListRow({ children, onClick, isSelected, showChevron, ...props }) {
  return (
    <Row
      minWidth="20rem"
      padding="3"
      alignItems="center"
      gap="3"
      borderColor="muted"
      border="bottom"
      backgroundColor={isSelected ? 'interactive' : undefined}
      className={onClick ? `cursor-pointer ${!isSelected ? 'hover:bg-interactive' : ''}` : ''}
      onClick={onClick}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
      {showChevron && <Icon size="sm" color="muted"><ChevronRight /></Icon>}
    </Row>
  );
}

export function ListRowAvatar({ src, fallback, size = 'md' }) {
  const sizeMap = { sm: '8', md: '10', lg: '12' };

  return (
    <Row
      width={sizeMap[size]}
      height={sizeMap[size]}
      borderRadius="full"
      backgroundColor="interactive"
      flexShrink="0"
      alignItems="center"
      justifyContent="center"
      overflow="hidden"
    >
      {src ? (
        <img src={src} alt="" style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%', objectFit: 'cover' }} />
      ) : (
        <Text color="muted" weight="medium">{fallback}</Text>
      )}
    </Row>
  );
}

export function ListRowContent({ title, description, meta }) {
  return (
    <Column gap="0" flexGrow="1" overflow="hidden">
      <Row alignItems="center" gap="2">
        <Box overflow="hidden" flexGrow="1">
          <Text weight="medium" truncate>{title}</Text>
        </Box>
        {meta && <Text color="muted">{meta}</Text>}
      </Row>
      {description && (
        <Box overflow="hidden">
          <Text color="muted" truncate>{description}</Text>
        </Box>
      )}
    </Column>
  );
}

export function ListRowActions({ children }) {
  return (
    <Row gap="1" alignItems="center" onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}>
      {children}
    </Row>
  );
}
```
</ExampleCode>

## Variations

### With chevron (navigation)

  <Box border borderRadius="lg" overflow="hidden">
    <ListRow showChevron>
      <Icon color="muted"><Lucide.Settings /></Icon>
      <ListRowContent title="Account Settings" description="Manage your account preferences" />
    </ListRow>
    <ListRow showChevron>
      <Icon color="muted"><Lucide.Bell /></Icon>
      <ListRowContent title="Notifications" description="Configure notification settings" />
    </ListRow>
    <ListRow showChevron>
      <Icon color="muted"><Lucide.Shield /></Icon>
      <ListRowContent title="Security" description="Password and authentication" />
    </ListRow>
  </Box>

```jsx
    <ListRowContent title="Notifications" description="Configure notification settings" />
  </ListRow>

```

### Simple list

    </ListRow>

    </ListRow>

      <ListRowContent title="image.png" description="Modified 3 days ago" />

```jsx

  </ListRow>

  </ListRow>
</Box>
```

    <ListRow isSelected>
      <ListRowAvatar fallback="A" />

    </ListRow>
    <ListRow>
      <ListRowAvatar fallback="B" />
      <ListRowContent title="Other Item" description="Click to select" />
    </ListRow>
  </Box>

```jsx

  <ListRow isSelected>
    <ListRowAvatar fallback="A" />
```
